title: scan_history.team_id is never written by any scan path, so team scan sharing is dead end to end while shipping a full UI for it
description: PATCH /api/v3/history/[id] destructures teamId at :267, authorizes it at :313-326 and writes it at :349-352. That is the only write path to scan_history.team_id (instrumentation.ts:928) in the entire codebase. Every INSERT INTO scan_history omits the column: app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:368, scan/crawl/route.ts:440, scan/bulk/route.ts:278, scan/authenticated/route.ts:469, scan/github/route.ts:252, lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.ts:280, lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:633. No UI ever sends teamId: the only PATCH bodies sent are {notes} (app/history/page.tsx:394) and {isPublic} (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:339); a repo-wide grep for 'share to team' / 'share with team' across .tsx returns zero. The sibling columns webhooks.team_id (instrumentation.ts:934) and scheduled_scans.team_id (:937) have the same shape: PATCH accepts teamId (webhooks/[id]/route.ts:201, schedules/route.ts:308) and no UI sends it.
impact: GET /api/v3/teams/member-scans queries WHERE user_id = $1 AND team_id = $2 (app/api/v3/teams/member-scans/route.ts:53-60) and can only ever return an empty array, yet the product ships a complete viewer for it with pagination (app/teams/page.tsx:469, components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx). Every getTeamResourceAccess team branch across history, share and report is unreachable. The feature is documented and sold at app/docs/teams/page.tsx:374-380. A paying team customer sees an empty panel with no explanation.
recommendation: Add a 'Share with team' control to components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx beside the existing 'Make private' item at :590, populated from getAssignableTeamIds with a 'Personal (private)' null option, plus a team column and filter on History. Add the same selector to the webhook and schedule rows on Profile > Developer. Alternatively decide the feature is not wanted and remove the columns, the read paths and the docs section.

title: POST /api/v3/scan makes about 14 sequential database round trips before it returns a scan id, reading the same users row four separate times
description: The route awaits its gates one after another, though nearly all are independent: `canMakeRequest` (line 201) -> `getDailyLimit` -> `getUserPlan` (lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:75, a `users LEFT JOIN gifted_subscriptions`) plus a `rate_limits` SUM; `checkConcurrentScanLimit` (line 223) -> `resolveConcurrentLimit` -> `getUserPlanLimits` -> `getUserPlan` again (2nd read of the same users row) plus a COUNT; `validateScanTarget` (line 276, a blocking `dns.lookup`); `checkAccessRules` (line 285, two sequential queries, see perf-23); `resolveScanIsPublic` (line 348) -> `SELECT scans_private_by_default FROM users WHERE id = $1` (lib/scanner/scan-privacy.ts:44, 3rd read); `reserveConcurrentScanSlot` (line 363) -> `resolveConcurrentLimit` -> `getUserPlan` a third time (4th read) then `pool.connect` + BEGIN + `pg_advisory_xact_lock` + COUNT + INSERT + COMMIT; `incrementDailyCountCapped` (line 397). `getSession` at line 151 has already fetched that same users row once more. The concurrency COUNT is also executed twice (lib/rate-limiting/concurrent-scans.ts:59 then :113).
impact: Roughly 14 serialized round trips plus one DNS resolution stand between the user clicking Scan and the server acknowledging it. On a co-located Postgres that is ~30ms; behind a managed instance or a connection pooler at 10-15ms RTT it is 150-250ms of dead time added to the front of every scan, before a single check has run. It also multiplies: app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts pays a large part of it per URL (see perf-18).
recommendation: Memoize `getUserPlan`/`getUserPlanLimits` per request (a small AsyncLocalStorage or request-scoped cache) so the users row is read once, and fold `scans_private_by_default` into that same read. Run the independent gates concurrently: `Promise.all([canMakeRequest, checkConcurrentScanLimit, validateScanTarget, checkAccessRules, resolveScanIsPublic])` and evaluate the results in the current priority order so error messages are unchanged. Drop the pre-check at line 223 now that `reserveConcurrentScanSlot` is authoritative.

title: Share-link expiry is fully implemented, enforced on every read path, and unreachable from the UI
description: The route accepts expiresInDays constrained to 7, 30, 90 or null (app/api/v3/history/[id]/share/route.ts:12, :21-32, :110-113, :142) and scan_history.share_expires_at (instrumentation.ts:1307) is enforced on every read path: app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:35, public-scans/route.ts:75, shares/route.ts:27. A repo-wide grep for expiresInDays outside app/api returns zero hits, and the share action POSTs no body at all (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:290). The Shares page already renders the expiry via formatExpiry (components/shares/shares-types.ts:34, called at components/shares/shares-row.tsx:114), so it permanently prints 'Never expires' for every row.
impact: Every share link ever created is unlimited. A user who shares a scan with a contractor or a client has no way to time-limit it, on a feature where time-limiting is the main security control. The UI already has a slot showing the value it can never set.
recommendation: Add an expiry select (Never / 7 days / 30 days / 90 days) to components/scanner/share-modal.tsx beside the existing publiclyListed switch at :135, and a 'Change expiry' item to the row menu on app/shares/page.tsx. Note drift-15 first: publiclyListed on POST is currently ignored for an existing live share, which will bite whoever adds expiry to the same request.

title: Eight of nine feature flags are server-only or gate only half their surface, leaving dead UI and running workers
description: Only FEATURE_PDF_REPORTS crosses to the browser (app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts:20,31 into use-client-config.ts into scan-actions-menu.tsx:545); a grep for each of the other eight in that route returns zero. Several also gate only half their surface, each verified individually: FEATURE_PDF_REPORTS hides the menu item but not the endpoint, since app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts has no getSetting reference and still serves ?format=pdf at :199-204; FEATURE_SCHEDULED_SCANS gates creation (schedules/route.ts:71) but not execution, since lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.ts reads only its own concurrency settings, so existing schedules fire forever after the flag is off; FEATURE_WEBHOOKS gates registration (webhooks/route.ts:53) but not delivery, since lib/webhooks/*.ts contains no flag reference; FEATURE_TEAMS gates only POST (teams/route.ts:57) while GET, PATCH, DELETE, members/route.ts and app/teams/page.tsx are all ungated, contradicting the registry help at :665-672. By contrast POSTURE_DIGEST_ENABLED (posture-digest.ts:220) and DOMAIN_REVERIFY_ENABLED (reverify-worker.ts:60) do gate their workers correctly.
impact: Disabling a feature leaves its UI fully present and its background work running. The user discovers the flag only via a 403 on submit, and scheduled scans and webhook deliveries continue to fire for a feature the operator believes is off.
recommendation: Plumb the remaining eight flags through app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts so the UI can hide disabled features, and add the flag check to each feature's worker and endpoint, following the POSTURE_DIGEST_ENABLED pattern.

title: TOTP seed stored plaintext at rest
description: users.totp_secret held the base32 TOTP seed unencrypted. DB read = full 2FA bypass.
recommendation: Route through encryptApiKey/decryptApiKey (AES-256-GCM). Added idempotent backfill on startup.

title: API-key daily cap race: concurrent requests bypass the limit
description: checkRateLimit + recordUsage were two separate statements. N concurrent requests at used=limit-1 all passed, all inserted.
recommendation: Single transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on api_keys.id; recordUsage() is now a no-op kept only for back-compat.

title: Discord OAuth tokens stored plaintext at rest
description: discord_connections.access_token and refresh_token were plaintext. DB read = Discord account takeover via refresh token.
recommendation: Encrypt via encryptApiKey; added getDiscordTokens() helper that decrypts inline; backfill migration on startup.

title: Password change did not invalidate other sessions
description: A stolen session cookie remained valid for the full 7-day TTL even after the legitimate user rotated their password.
recommendation: Mirror reset-password: deleteAllSessions + createSession(current).

title: There is no overall A+ to F grade, so the badge and public host report speak safe/caution/unsafe and cannot occupy the vocabulary SecurityHeaders.com just vacated
category: list (a) gap rank 3: the grading vocabulary and the badge flywheel
description: Four of the free peers grade a whole site on one A+ to F scale: MDN HTTP Observatory (A+ down to F, ten header tests), SecurityHeaders.com (A+ to F on response headers), Qualys SSL Labs (A+ to F plus T and M), and ImmuniWeb (grade-gated PDF certificate plus installable badge). VulnRadar has the scoring machinery but not the vocabulary. lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:1 already computes a real SSL-Labs-style A+/A/B/C/D/F letter, but only for the TLS handshake. The whole-scan verdict is a three-state safety rating (lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:19, "safe" | "caution" | "unsafe") plus a 0-10 danger score (:306), and the embeddable badge renders exactly that three-state label (app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:99 to :115). Confirmed live this session: Snyk shut down the securityheaders.com API in April 2026 (announced January 2026), leaving only the free web scanner; the replacements ranking for "securityheaders alternative" are unknown micro-vendors (WebAudit, Guardr, detectzestack, myssl.info, sitesecurityscore). SSL Labs v4 requires an organizational email and forbids commercial use by default, and MDN Observatory dropped TLS entirely in October 2024. The auto-updating badge infrastructure already exists and is idempotent per (user, url) so an embed never breaks (app/api/v3/badge/site/route.ts:8).
impact: A README badge that says "caution" is a liability the owner removes; a badge that says "A" is a trophy the owner keeps and that links back. ImmuniWeb built 380M+ scans on exactly that mechanic and gates the certificate on the grade so people work to earn it. VulnRadar has the badge, the public host page, the API, and TLS plus DNS plus header coverage that the vacated SecurityHeaders niche wants, and cannot be compared against the incumbent because it does not speak the incumbent's scale.
recommendation: Add `getSiteGrade(findings): "A+"|"A"|"B"|"C"|"D"|"F"` to lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts, derived from the existing danger score and severity weights so it stays deterministic and needs no new detection work, and document the exact deduction table on a public page the way lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:20 already documents its own. Render the grade as the primary label in app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:99 (keep safe/caution/unsafe as the badge's secondary colour semantics), lead with it on app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx, and gate the shareable badge on B or better, matching ImmuniWeb. Then publish a keyless or free-key-tier grading endpoint documented in app/docs/api as the drop-in for the dead securityheaders.com API, using the existing demo-scan rate-limit shape (app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:97) rather than the account-gated /api/v3/scan.

title: Ticketing stops at one one-way GitHub issue holding up to 50 findings, with no per-finding issue, no close-the-loop retest, and no Jira or Linear
category: list (a) gap rank 8: issue tracker integration
description: Jira is universal across all eight commercial vendors, Slack near-universal, and the real differentiator is two-way sync: Detectify's Jira integration updates the finding when the ticket is resolved, and Probely/Snyk goes further, marking the Jira issue Done automatically triggers a retest of that finding. Linear appears only at Intruder (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "Table stakes" item 2). VulnRadar's entire ticketing surface is POST /api/v3/scan/github-issue (app/api/v3/scan/github-issue/route.ts:11), which files one issue per scan into one repo, listing at most 50 findings in the body (`MAX_FINDINGS_LISTED = 50`, :26). It is one-way and one-shot: nothing reads the issue's state back, nothing closes it when a rescan shows the finding gone, and there is no per-finding issue so no finding has its own trackable ticket. Notification delivery is limited to Discord, Slack and generic webhooks (lib/webhooks/detect-type.ts:7 to :14) plus email; there is no Jira, Linear, ServiceNow or Teams destination anywhere in lib/.
impact: For the developer this product targets, a single 50-item issue is a dump, not a workflow: it cannot be assigned, prioritised, or closed piecemeal, and once one finding is fixed the issue is stale but still open. For the small security team, the absence of any close-the-loop mechanism means the remediation state lives only inside VulnRadar (lib/scanner/remediation-store.ts) and inside the tracker separately, and the two drift.
recommendation: Do not start with Jira. The GitHub connection already exists, is already authorised for issue writes (lib/github/github-connections.ts), and the finding IDs are already stable across runs (lib/scanner/_helpers.ts generateId, `<checkId>--<urlHash>`), which is exactly what a close-the-loop integration needs and what Jira would still need built. Extend app/api/v3/scan/github-issue/route.ts with a per-finding mode: one issue per finding, titled with the check id, labelled by severity, and stamped with the stable finding id in the body. Then in lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts, which already diffs a completed scan against the previous scan of the same URL by that same id, close any tracked issue whose finding is absent from the new scan and post a one-line comment saying which scan proved it fixed. That is the Probely/Snyk retest loop, built on machinery that already exists. Add Jira only if a paying user asks for it by name.

title: The self-updater advertises itself as supported inside Docker but writes into a root-owned /app as uid 1001, runs a migrate script the image does not contain, and any success is discarded by the documented update command
description: Static trace. isUpdaterSupported() (lib/updater/environment.ts:8-17) returns unsupported only when process.env.VERCEL is set; there is no container detection, so both app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts:37 and .../apply/route.ts:56 report the updater available inside the official image and the admin UI offers it. runUpdateJob then sets appRoot = process.cwd() (lib/updater/apply.ts:206), which is /app, and calls copyTreeOverlay(sourceRoot, appRoot) at :261 to write the release's full source tree there. /app is root:root because WORKDIR /app runs as root at Dockerfile:68 and the process runs as USER nextjs (uid 1001) from :102, so creating new top-level entries such as /app/lib or /app/app fails with EACCES, while pre-existing chowned files such as /app/package.json and /app/next.config.mjs would be overwritten in place first (overwriting an existing file needs write on the file, not the directory). The job then fails with a raw permission error after package.json has already been replaced with the new release's copy while node_modules and .next are still the old build. Even if the copy succeeded, the npm-ci step at :325 and the `npm run db:migrate -- --yes` step at :353 run against a tree with no scripts/ (host-02), and the final log line at :369 asks the admin to run `npm run build` and restart, which in a container means the next `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` (app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684) throws the whole writable layer away. AUDIT-013#cov-06 recorded that this pipeline has 0% test coverage and AUDIT-013#migrate-01 that the migrate step it invokes stamps 3.0.0 on a schema missing 11 tables; this finding is about the updater being reachable at all in the deployment shape where it cannot work.
impact: A self-hosting admin sees an in-app Update button, clicks it, and gets a half-applied file copy plus an opaque EACCES in the job log, with package.json now describing a version whose code is not installed. In the worst case they then follow the log's advice and restart, and the update silently disappears on the next image pull.
recommendation: Extend isUpdaterSupported() in lib/updater/environment.ts to detect a container (existence of /.dockerenv, or an explicit CONTAINER/VULNRADAR_UPDATER_DISABLED env var set in the Dockerfile) and return supported: false with a reason pointing at `docker compose pull`. If in-container updating is wanted instead, chown /app to nextjs:nodejs in the runner stage and ship scripts/ (host-02).

title: Four security-relevant rate limits are inline numeric literals that never reach the admin registry, unlike the seventeen that do
description: lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:247-:276 exposes seventeen named rate limits, each carrying a `limit` name so checkRateLimit resolves the live admin override (registry keys RATE_LIMIT_*_MAX_ATTEMPTS / _WINDOW_MINUTES). Four call sites bypass that entirely by passing raw numbers: app/api/v3/auth/forgot-password/route.ts:49-:53 (per-email reset cap, maxAttempts 3 / windowSeconds 60*60), app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:130-:134 (per-email signup cap, 5 / 60*60), app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:69-:73 (domain add, 20 / 3600) and app/api/v3/domains/[id]/verify/route.ts:39-:42 (domain verify, 30 / 3600). None of the four has a registry key. This is distinct from AUDIT-009#dup-01, which was about routes importing the wrong RATE_LIMITS export; lib/config/constants.ts:352-:360 records that collision as resolved. These four never reference either export.
impact: An operator responding to a signup-flood or reset-flood incident can tighten every limiter in the admin panel and still leave the two per-email counters, which are the ones that actually stop the attack described in each site's own comment, at their compiled values. The two domain limiters are the documented numbers in app/docs/api/page.tsx:843 and :876, so the docs also become uneditable truth.
recommendation: Add four entries to RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULTS and RATE_LIMITS (forgotPasswordEmail, signupEmail, domainAdd, domainVerify) in lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts with matching registry keys, then spread them at the four call sites the way every other limiter does.

title: Plan copy sells raw numbers and platitudes instead of what a user can do, and the checkout page advertises a 30 and 90 day scan history that no plan actually has
description: lib/billing/catalog.ts descriptions are the copy that appears under each plan name at components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:83-85: "For individuals exploring security scanning" (:103), "Support VulnRadar development + 100 scans/day" (:133), "For power users - 150 scans/day" (:166), "Maximum power - 500 scans/day" (:198). "For power users" and "Maximum power" are exactly the adjective-only benefit claims CLAUDE.md bans, and none of the four says what the extra scans let you do. The feature bullets are the same shape: "Full vulnerability detection", "Security headers analysis", "SSL/TLS checks", "API access" (:106-109) are category nouns with no consequence attached, and every one of them is true on every plan, so the free card spends four of its eight bullets on things that are not differentiators. Separately there is a factual error. CONFIG_BILLING_FREE_RETENTION through CONFIG_BILLING_ELITE_SUPPORTER_RETENTION are all -1, meaning unlimited (lib/config/config-values.ts:1209-1212), yet catalog.ts:110 still says "30-day scan history" and :137 says "90-day scan history". app/pricing/page.tsx:44 strips those strings with a /scan history/i filter, but app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:280 renders plan.features.slice(0, 5) with no filter, so the Core checkout page, the highest-intent page in the funnel, tells a buyer they are getting 90-day history when every plan including free already keeps everything. catalog.ts:170 then sells "Unlimited scan history" as a Pro upgrade over Core, which the free tier also has. Finally components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:78-79 renders a "Most picked" badge driven by the hardcoded `popular: libPlan.id === "pro_supporter"` at app/pricing/page.tsx:55, which is a claim about other customers' behaviour that is not measured from anything.
impact: A visitor cannot tell what changes when they pay, because the cards restate the same nouns at four price points and the one concrete difference they do state, retention, is wrong on the checkout page and identical across plans in reality. The Pro card's headline upgrade is something the free tier already includes. "Most picked" is an unbacked social-proof claim on a product with roughly 50 users, which is the kind of thing that is cheap to remove and expensive if noticed.
recommendation: Rewrite the four descriptions in lib/billing/catalog.ts in terms of what the tier lets you do: free (:103) "25 scans a day. Enough to keep an eye on everything you personally ship." core_supporter (:133) "100 scans a day and two running at once, for someone watching more than one property." pro_supporter (:166) "150 scans a day, a team of three, and 5,000 API calls a day. Enough to gate a real pipeline." elite_supporter (:198) "500 scans a day, unlimited webhooks and schedules, teams of ten. For an agency or a portfolio." Rewrite the free bullets (:105-114) to "Every check on every plan, nothing held back behind a tier", "25 scans a day, one at a time", "Unlimited history, diff any two runs", "5 URLs per bulk call, 3 schedules, 1 webhook", "REST API and one bearer token", "PDF, JSON, SARIF and Markdown export". Delete the "30-day scan history" string at :110 and "90-day scan history" at :137 outright so getRetentionLabel in app/pricing/page.tsx:26-31 is the only source, which also repairs the checkout page without touching it, and drop "Unlimited scan history" from the Pro list at :170 since it is not an upgrade. Either replace the "Most picked" badge at components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:78-79 with a factual label such as "Recommended", or drive `popular` from a real distribution query.

title: Nothing replaces the removed timer: the status endpoint returns progress but no findings, so the wait has no payoff until it ends
category: scanning page: replacement for the timer
description:
This is the replacement proposal AUDIT-011#scan-05 asked for and did not specify. It is scoped strictly to what the API produces today, verified by reading the endpoint and the producer.

WHAT EXISTS NOW. GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id] builds `responseBody` at app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts:162-168 with exactly five keys while a scan is live: `status`, `currentCategory`, `categoriesCompleted`, `categoriesTotal`, `elapsedMs`. On `completed` it adds the whole `result`; on `failed` it adds `error`. The client reads three of them (app/dashboard/page.tsx:146-150) and drops `elapsedMs` on the floor. The producer is `createProgressTracker` in lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139, whose hook fires once per CATEGORY as `start` and once as `done`, writing `current_category` / `categories_completed` / `categories_total` to scan_history. The hook's type is `(category: string, phase) => void` (lib/scanner/types.ts:352-355): it carries no check count and no findings.

So of the three things the brief asked for, the API supports exactly one and a half today:
1. "Which check category is running" -- SUPPORTED. `currentCategory` is a real Category id, and lib/scanner/category-meta.ts already holds a client-safe label and one-line blurb for all 18, importing only a type.
2. "How many of the ~797 checks are done" -- NOT SUPPORTED as checks; supported as families. `categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal` is real and exact (route.ts:332-339 derives the denominator from `getPlannedSyncCategories` plus `getPlannedAsyncBranches`, never estimated). Per-check counts are computed but only at the end: lib/scanner/engine.ts:206-211 returns `checksRun` and `checksSkipped` after the whole loop, and they reach the user only as the "Checks run" stat on the finished view (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:295-302).
3. "Findings streaming in as discovered" -- NOT SUPPORTED AT ALL. `runSyncChecks` accumulates into a local `findings` array (engine.ts:156) and nothing reads it until `dedupeFindings` at :205. scan_history.findings is written once, by `finalizeScanSuccess` (scan-jobs.ts:240-245), in the same UPDATE that flips status to `completed`. There is no partial-findings column and no partial-findings field on the poll response.
impact: After scanui-01 the card would show a family name, a bar, and nothing else, which is less information than the clock it replaced. The scan is the product's whole value proposition and for its entire duration the user is shown zero of its output, then all of it at once, then (until AUDIT-011#scan-08 is fixed) a blur over the top of it. The visible work is a large part of a scanner's perceived worth and this page currently spends the wait proving nothing.
recommendation:
Build it in three tiers, each independently shippable.

TIER 1, zero backend change, ship with scanui-01. Three real numbers in a mono definition list, all already on the wire:
  FAMILIES  12 / 18      (categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal)
  RUNNING   DNS          (CATEGORY_META[currentCategory].label)
  NEXT      Email        (the next entry in the client's own planned family list)
plus the one-line `FAMILY_STEP` sentence for the running family, which is already written and is good copy ("Grepping responses for keys and tokens"). Keep those strings; they are the best thing in the current component.

TIER 2, one generated file, still no server change, gives a real check count. scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs already iterates lib/scanner/checks-data/<category>.json per category (see its loop and the write at :283-286) and emits lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts, which is client-safe (`EXACT_CHECK_COUNT = 797`, `EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT = 18`, no runtime imports). Add one export: `export const EXACT_CHECKS_BY_CATEGORY: Record<string, number> = {...}`. The client then sums the counts of the families already marked done and renders `CHECKS 531 / 797` in `font-mono tabular-nums`, rising in real steps. Label it honestly: this counts the checks in the families that have reported, so it will slightly overstate against the final `checksRun` (page checks whose `requirementsMet` gate fails are counted as skipped at engine.ts:186-188). Either accept a final reconciliation to the real `checksRun`, or emit legacy-only counts and label the row `RULES`.

TIER 3, the real prize, and it needs a backend change. Stream findings as they are discovered:
  a) Widen `ScanProgressHook` (lib/scanner/types.ts:352-355) to `(category, phase, snapshot?: { found: number; newFindings: { severity: Severity; title: string }[] })`.
  b) In lib/scanner/engine.ts, at the `onProgress?.(category, "done")` call at :203, pass the findings pushed during that category's iteration (the loop already has them; slice `findings` from the index recorded before `onProgress?.(category, "start")` at :166).
  c) In `createProgressTracker` (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139) append those into a new `scan_history.partial_findings JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` column in the same fire-and-forget UPDATE that already runs there, keeping the existing `WHERE status IN ('pending','running')` guard so a late write after completion is a no-op. Add the column in instrumentation.ts beside the other scan_history additions, and to scripts/migrate (see AUDIT-013#migrate-01: this is exactly the kind of column that gets missed).
  d) In app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts add `responseBody.partialFindings = row.partial_findings` in the live branch only (never in the `completed` branch, where `result.findings` is authoritative). Cap it server-side at ~40 entries and store only `{severity, title}`, never evidence or remediation, so a 2-second poll stays small.
  e) On completion, clear `partial_findings` in `finalizeScanSuccess`'s UPDATE so a re-poll of a finished scan does not carry two lists.
The one honesty trap: `dedupeFindings` (engine.ts:205) runs after the last category, so a streamed count can go DOWN at the end. Present the live list under the label "Found so far" and let the completed view's real summary replace it wholesale, rather than animating a number downward.

What NOT to do: do not synthesise a percentage from `elapsedMs`, and do not use `elapsedMs` at all on this screen. It is the same number scanui-01 removes, just served from the server.

title: Leaving the scanning page abandons the scan with no way back, and the in-flight row then renders in Recent scans and History as a finished scan with 0 findings in 0ms
category: scanning page: navigate away and back
description:
The scan's entire progress state lives in the DashboardContent component: `status`, `runningScanId` and `scanProgress` are all `useState` (app/dashboard/page.tsx:204, 219, 234) and the poll loop is a local `async` function. There is no persistence, no `sessionStorage`, and nothing that queries for the user's own in-flight scans. So a soft navigation, a refresh, or a phone backgrounding the tab long enough to be evicted drops the whole thing: coming back to /dashboard shows `status === "idle"`, the empty scan form, and no indication that a scan of theirs is still running server-side. It does keep running (that is the point of the background-job design, see app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:405-419) and it does eventually complete, so the user has no way to watch it and no signal that watching would even be possible.

What they see instead is worse than nothing. The row is INSERTed as `pending` before any work starts (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:365-379) and `scan_history.scanned_at` defaults to `NOW()` (instrumentation.ts:428), so it exists immediately and sorts to the top of every list ordered by `scanned_at DESC`. Neither list filters on status:
  - app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:41-44 selects `public_id AS id, url, summary, findings_count, duration, scanned_at, source FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY scanned_at DESC LIMIT $2`, with no `status` predicate. This feeds the "Recent scans" widget on the very page the user just came back to (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx).
  - app/api/v3/history/route.ts:120-139 has the same shape and the same omission (`WHERE sh.user_id = $1 AND (sh.scan_type IS NULL OR sh.scan_type != 'github')`).
The column defaults at instrumentation.ts:420-423 are `summary '{}'`, `findings_count 0`, `duration 0`, and `finalizeScanSuccess` (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:244-248) is the only thing that fills them. So a running scan, a cancelled scan (`finalizeScanFailure` at :363-381 sets `status='failed'` but never touches `summary` or `findings_count`) and a watchdog-killed scan all render identically to a genuinely clean result: the site's name, "0 findings", "0.0s".
impact: The most natural recovery action, going back to the scanner, is punished twice: the user loses the scan they were watching, and the page they land on tells them that scan found nothing. On a phone, where the browser evicting a background tab is routine, this is the normal path rather than the edge case. A cancelled scan leaves the same false clean-bill-of-health row permanently.
recommendation:
Two changes, independently useful.

1. Make the lists honest. Add `status` to both SELECTs (app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:41 and app/api/v3/history/route.ts:120 and :129) and render non-completed rows distinctly rather than as zero-finding results: `running` and `pending` get a muted "Running" chip in place of the findings summary, `failed` gets a `text-[hsl(var(--severity-medium))]` "Did not finish" chip. Do not filter them out, because a user needs to see that a scan happened; just stop them wearing a clean result's clothes. Check whether the aggregate queries in the same file (the severity roll-up at :46-54 and the top-findings query at :55-63) should also exclude non-completed rows; they sum over `summary` and `findings`, which are `'{}'`/`'[]'` for those rows, so they are currently harmless but will silently break if partial findings are ever stored (see scanui-02 tier 3).

2. Let the user rejoin a running scan. `GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id]` already returns everything needed and is already owner-scoped (`getOwnedScan`). Either (a) write the in-flight `scanId` to `sessionStorage` in `runScan` right after `setRunningScanId(scanId)` (page.tsx:594), clear it in the `finally` at :620-622, and on mount resume `pollScanStatus` against it if the row is still `pending`/`running`, or (b) add a `?scan_job=<publicId>` param that the existing `syncFromUrl` effect (page.tsx:302-342) recognises as a third meaning alongside target and history-id. Option (a) is smaller and survives a plain refresh; option (b) additionally makes the running scan linkable. Either way the recovered state should render the same readout scanui-03 specifies, so nothing new has to be designed for it.

title: The two Stripe events that reverse money, charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created, are the only two of nine handled event types with no test
description: app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts measures 68.18% statements and 58.3% branches over 264 statements. The handler switch has nine cases: checkout.session.completed (183), customer.subscription.created (296), updated (475), deleted (626), invoice.payment_succeeded (686), invoice.payment_failed (770), payment_intent.succeeded (803), charge.refunded (940), charge.dispute.created (982). Extracting the event-type string literals from tests/app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.test.ts yields eight, and the two missing are charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created. Those two branches each call reverseAiCreditPurchase, reverseGithubCreditPurchase, and reverseBrowserbaseCreditPurchase in a Promise.all (lines 958-962 and 997-1001). The reversal functions themselves are well covered (lib/billing/ai-usage.ts 98.27%, browserbase-usage.ts 100%, github-review-usage.ts 98.59%), so what is untested is the wiring: the partial-refund early-break at line 947, the payment_intent extraction that must handle both a string and an expanded object (lines 953-956 and 989-992), and the dispatch itself. lib/billing/stripe-webhook-setup.ts:29-30 does register both events with Stripe, and tests/lib/billing/stripe-webhook-setup.test.ts covers REQUIRED_EVENTS, but nothing asserts the REQUIRED_EVENTS list and the switch labels agree.
impact: If either case label is renamed, or the payment_intent extraction breaks when Stripe sends an expanded object rather than a string, a refunded or charged-back customer keeps every AI token, GitHub review token, and Browserbase second they paid for. That is direct revenue loss on the exact transactions where the money has already left, and it is silent: the webhook still returns 200, the reversal functions still pass their own unit tests, and the only evidence is a console.log that never fires.
recommendation: Add two describes to tests/app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.test.ts. For charge.refunded assert: refunded:false logs and reverses nothing; refunded:true with a string payment_intent calls all three reverse functions with that id; refunded:true with an expanded payment_intent object extracts .id. For charge.dispute.created assert the same extraction and the three reverse calls. Add one drift test asserting the set of `case` labels in the route equals REQUIRED_EVENTS in lib/billing/stripe-webhook-setup.ts, so registering an event without handling it (or vice versa) fails.

title: The Browserbase client is at 16.87% and page-screenshot at 7.44%, leaving the session-teardown call that stops a paid third-party meter untested at all three of its call sites
description: lib/browserbase/client.ts is the largest sub-50% file in the tree: 243 statements at 16.87% statements / 27.05%-adjacent branches, 662 lines, ten exports (createBrowserSession:112, getBrowserSession:165, getBrowserLiveUrls:189, endBrowserSession:213, pickLiveViewerUrl:273, isBrowserBaseConfigured:279, navigateBrowserSession:298, openCdpPageSession:416, getBrowserSessionLogs:573, parseNetworkRequests:594). tests/lib/browserbase/ contains one file, concurrency-queue.test.ts, which tests a different module. lib/browserbase/network-capture.ts is at 27.05% and lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts at 7.44% (94 statements, 21.42% functions). endBrowserSession has three call sites that must run or the session keeps billing: app/api/v3/browser/sessions/route.ts:199 (the create-failed cleanup) and :325 (explicit delete), lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts:560, and lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts:267. None of those teardown paths is exercised.
impact: Browserbase is a real paid third party billed by session-seconds, and the credit ledger charges the user for it. A regression where the teardown is skipped on an error path (the exact shape of the route.ts:199 cleanup) leaks a live session per failed scan. Nothing in the product notices: the scan reports a normal failure, the user is charged whatever the ledger recorded, and the overage shows up on the operator's Browserbase invoice at the end of the month. sessions/route.ts:199 already writes `.catch(() => {})`, so even a thrown teardown error is swallowed.
recommendation: Add tests/lib/browserbase/client.test.ts mocking the Browserbase HTTP boundary and assert createBrowserSession sends keepAlive:true, endBrowserSession issues the delete for the right id, and openCdpPageSession honours its timeout argument. Then add teardown assertions at the three call sites: in tests/app/api/v3/browser/sessions/route.test.ts assert endBrowserSession is called when the post-create work throws, and add a page-screenshot test asserting endBrowserSession runs in the failure path as well as the success path.

title: Two auth crypto primitives are copy-pasted rather than shared: generateBackupCodes exists verbatim in both 2FA routes with its security rationale already diverged, and the HMAC signed-token sign/verify pair is duplicated across pending-2fa and ipv4-echo-token with two different freshness contracts
description:
generateBackupCodes is defined identically in app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:22 and app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:11: same `count = 8`, same `crypto.randomBytes(10)`, same hex/uppercase, same XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX split. Both carry a copy of the comment recording a prior hardening ("10 bytes (80 bits) per code. The previous `randomBytes(4)` (32 bits) is below NIST 800-63B guidance for backup verification codes"), and the comment itself has already drifted: the setup.ts copy adds "The 2FA verify endpoint rate-limits to 5 attempts per 5 minutes per user+IP, so 32-bit codes were computationally in scope" and the backup-codes.ts copy does not. Nothing links the two, so a future change to code length, alphabet, or count applies to enrolment or to regeneration but not both, and the two paths would then mint differently shaped codes into the same column.

Separately, lib/auth/pending-2fa.ts and lib/auth/ipv4-echo-token.ts each implement the whole signed-token primitive: signingKey() reading and length-checking API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY (pending-2fa.ts:24, ipv4-echo-token.ts:24), computeTag() as HMAC-SHA256 over `${HMAC_DOMAIN}.${payloadB64}` with the same codeql suppression comment (pending-2fa.ts:34, ipv4-echo-token.ts:34), and a verify half that splits on the last dot, length-checks, timingSafeEquals the tag and base64url-JSON-decodes the payload (pending-2fa.ts:59-77, ipv4-echo-token.ts:66-92). ipv4-echo-token.ts:17 states the relationship outright: "Format mirrors lib/auth/pending-2fa.ts: base64url(json).base64url(hmac)." Only the domain string differs, and the two have already diverged on their security contract: verifyIpv4Token enforces max-age and a clock-skew floor inline (ipv4-echo-token.ts:88-90), while verifyPendingToken enforces no freshness at all and delegates it to callers (pending-2fa.ts:57).
impact: A fix to either primitive is applied to one site and silently missed on the other. For generateBackupCodes that means one of the two 2FA paths keeps weaker codes after the next hardening. For the token pair it means a padding, canonicalization, or replay fix to one signed-token format leaves the other exposed, and the split freshness contract is exactly the kind of asymmetry that produces a replay window: any new caller of verifyPendingToken that forgets its own `ts` check gets an eternally valid token, while the identically shaped ipv4 token cannot be replayed past 120 seconds.
recommendation: Move generateBackupCodes into lib/auth/ (next to the existing 2FA helpers) and import it in both app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:22 and app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:11. Extract the signed-token primitive into one module, for example lib/auth/signed-token.ts exporting `sign(domain, payload)` and `verify(domain, token, { maxAgeMs })`, and rewrite lib/auth/pending-2fa.ts and lib/auth/ipv4-echo-token.ts as thin domain-specific wrappers over it; make maxAgeMs required so a new caller cannot accidentally get the no-freshness behaviour.

title: The documented 1 MiB request-body cap lives inside parseBody, which only 19 of the 73 body-reading routes use; the other 54 call request.json() directly and there is no global limit behind them
category: guard applied to a subset of siblings
description:
lib/api/api-utils.ts:170-176 documents the cap as a deliberate fix: "L-10: Hard cap on JSON request bodies. Without this, a client can send a multi-GB JSON body that the server will buffer before rejecting. 1 MiB is more than enough for our route shapes." It is enforced only inside parseBody (lib/api/api-utils.ts:181-228), which checks content-length against MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES at :188-196 before calling request.json().

I split every route.ts under app/api by which one it uses. 19 files call parseBody, 54 call `request.json()` or `req.json()` directly, and the two sets do not overlap at all. The 19 are almost entirely under app/api/v3/auth/, app/api/v3/account/, plus keys, browser/sessions, admin/staff-invites and admin/updater/apply, which is the shape of a fix applied by directory and never extended. The 54 include the whole scan surface (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts, scan/bulk, scan/crawl, scan/verify-batch, scan/import-spec, scan/remediation/bulk), the whole teams and support-ticket surface, app/api/v3/admin/route.ts, app/api/v3/webhooks/route.ts, app/api/v3/domains/route.ts, and the two contact forms.

There is no backstop underneath them: I checked next.config.mjs and middleware.ts and neither sets a body size limit, and Next.js App Router route handlers have no default one (the Pages Router's 1 MB bodyParser limit does not apply). app/api/v3/account/unsubscribe/route.ts is in PUBLIC_PATHS (lib/config/public-paths.ts:178) and reads its body raw, so at least one uncapped route is reachable with no session.
impact: Any signed-in account (signup is open) can POST an arbitrarily large JSON body to app/api/v3/scan/route.ts or any of the other 53 routes and the server buffers it in memory before any validation runs. On a deployment sized for ~50 users, a few concurrent multi-hundred-megabyte bodies are enough to OOM the process. The narrower and more likely cost is maintenance: the cap is written down as a security requirement in one helper that 74% of the body-reading routes do not go through, so the requirement is not actually a property of the API.
recommendation: Do not try to convert 54 handlers. Add the content-length check to middleware.ts for any request to /api/ with a method that carries a body, using the same MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES value exported from lib/api/api-utils.ts, and return 413 there. Then parseBody's own check becomes a redundant second line rather than the only one, and a new route cannot opt out by forgetting to call it.

title: The relative-time consolidation missed three call sites, and two of them reintroduce verbatim the exact two defects the shared module's own doc comment says it was written to fix
description:
lib/ui/relative-time.ts:22-31 documents a completed consolidation and names the defects it removed: "The single source for this format: previously ~10 near-identical copies had drifted (some read '0m ago' instead of 'just now', one never fell back to a date and read '92d ago' forever, and the date fallback varied between 'Aug 12' and '8/12/2026')." formatRelativeTime (:32-52) is the survivor, re-exported through components/admin/utils.ts:123 and components/assets/assets-types.ts:25 with "Canonical relative-time formatter" comments.

Three files still hand-roll it, and two of them are the two named defects:

1. components/admin/features/support-inbox.tsx:68 `timeAgo` ends at `return \`${Math.round(hrs / 24)}d ago\`` with no date fallback. That is the "read '92d ago' forever" bug, restored.
2. components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:65 `timeAgo` falls back at 30 days to `new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString()`, which renders "8/12/2026". That is the "varied between 'Aug 12' and '8/12/2026'" bug, restored; the canonical formatter falls back at 7 days to `toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric" })`, i.e. "Aug 12".

These two render the same objects. support-inbox.tsx is the staff view of a support ticket and support-tickets.tsx is the user's view of the same ticket, so one ticket's "last activity" reads "412d ago" to staff and "8/12/2026" to the user. The same pair also duplicates STATUS_STYLES and StatusBadge (support-inbox.tsx:79, support-tickets.tsx:89, identical bodies).

3. components/scanner/subdomain-discovery.tsx:92 defines a private `formatAge` even though lib/ui/relative-time.ts:8 exports one, and lib/ui/relative-time.ts:2-4 names this very component as its consumer: "shared by the result panels that show freshness (subdomain discovery, DNS records, port sweep). Matches the wording SubdomainDiscovery introduced." The two sibling panels do import it (components/scanner/port-scan-panel.tsx:22, components/scanner/dns-records-panel.tsx:24), and subdomain-discovery.tsx:22 imports formatRefreshAvailability from that same module in the same statement while shadowing formatAge. The bodies are currently identical, so this one is a live divergence risk rather than a current bug. A third, unrelated `formatAge(ageMs: number | null)` exists at components/admin/features/queue-status-utils.ts:41, so the name means two things.
impact: Staff triaging the support inbox see ages like "412d ago" that are unreadable as dates, on the one screen where knowing when a ticket last moved matters. The same ticket shows the user a different format. Beyond that, the consolidation is not actually done: the module presents itself as the single source and is not, so the next timestamp change is applied once and misses three screens, exactly as it did the last time.
recommendation: Delete components/admin/features/support-inbox.tsx:68 and components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:65 and import formatRelativeTime from @/lib/ui/relative-time in both. Delete components/scanner/subdomain-discovery.tsx:92 and use the exported formatAge already imported alongside formatRefreshAvailability at :22. Rename components/admin/features/queue-status-utils.ts:41 to formatAgeMs so the name is unambiguous. Hoist the shared StatusBadge and STATUS_STYLES out of the two support components into components/contact/ or a shared module.

title: Extends AUDIT-012#obs-09 with the success-shape half: GET responses use four different envelopes, three routes return a bare array, one paginated route names its count totalTeams while its three siblings use total, and lib/api/client.ts is imported by 2 files while 94 call fetch directly
description:
AUDIT-012#obs-09 inventoried the ERROR shapes (five of them, 117 of 155 routes bypassing ApiResponse/withErrorHandling). It did not cover the success side or the client side. I extracted the last success return from every GET handler in app/api (56 of them) and grouped them.

Envelopes in use:
  1. Named-key object, the majority: `{ shares }`, `{ teams }`, `{ tickets }`, `{ notifications }`, `{ feedback }`, `{ teammates }`, `{ invitations }`, `{ remediation }`, `{ summaries }`, `{ repos }`.
  2. Bare array, no envelope: app/api/v3/schedules/route.ts:60 (`result.rows`), app/api/v3/webhooks/route.ts:42 (`result.rows`), app/api/v3/badge/scans/route.ts (`scans`). A client cannot add a sibling field to these without a breaking change.
  3. `{ success: true, data: {...} }`: app/api/v3/checkout/verify-subscription/route.ts. Nothing else uses it, and app/api/v3/finding-types/route.ts uses `{ success: false, error }` for its failure but a bare object for its success, so `success` is not a reliable discriminator anywhere.
  4. Flat top-level fields with no envelope at all: app/api/v3/billing/route.ts, app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts, app/api/version/route.ts, app/api/v3/health/route.ts.

Pagination envelope keys diverge on one route: app/api/v3/admin/content/route.ts, app/api/v3/admin/email-logs/route.ts and app/api/v3/admin/error-logs/route.ts all return `{ <items>, page, totalPages, total }`, and app/api/v3/admin/teams/route.ts:71 returns `totalTeams` instead of `total` for the identical concept. components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:107 reads `data.total || 0` to drive its "N total" footer; that pattern silently renders 0 against the teams endpoint, which is why components/admin/teams/teams-list.tsx:646 only consumes totalPages and drops the count. app/api/v3/admin/route.ts returns `total` with no page/totalPages at all.

The query-parameter side is, for the record, consistent: all seven paginated routes take `page` and `limit`, no route uses offset or cursor, so there is nothing to fix there.

On the client, lib/api/client.ts:44-49 is the shared reader that normalises `errorData.error` and falls back to the literal `API error: <status>`. It is imported by exactly 2 files under app/ and components/, while 94 files call `fetch(` directly and each re-implements its own `data.error || "Something went wrong"` handling. So the normalisation obs-09 recommends adopting has no adoption to build on.
impact: Every new client call site has to discover, per endpoint, whether the payload is the array itself, a named key, `data`, or flat fields, and whether the count is `total` or `totalTeams`. That is why the teams list drops its result count and why 94 files each carry their own error-unwrapping block. The three bare-array endpoints (schedules, webhooks, badge/scans) cannot gain pagination or a count without breaking their callers. Documented in app/docs/api, these inconsistencies are also the public API surface, so third-party integrators hit them too.
recommendation: Pick the named-key envelope as canonical, since it is already the majority, and write it down in app/docs/api. Fix the three cheap deviants first: wrap app/api/v3/schedules/route.ts:60 and app/api/v3/webhooks/route.ts:42 as `{ schedules }` / `{ webhooks }` (both have exactly one client each, in components/profile/tabs/developer/), rename app/api/v3/admin/teams/route.ts:71 `totalTeams` to `total`, and convert app/api/v3/checkout/verify-subscription/route.ts off the lone `{ success, data }` shape. Then extend lib/api/client.ts to return the unwrapped payload and migrate call sites by directory, starting with components/profile/ where nine of them already duplicate the same error block.

title: Report export has no rate limiter on the session path and builds the PDF synchronously over an uncapped findings array
description: GET /api/v3/history/[id]/report?format=pdf reaches `Buffer.from(generatePdfReport(result))` at app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:200. generatePdfReport (lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:11) is a synchronous pure-JS PDF builder that iterates every finding with nested word-wrap loops (:321 `for (let i = 0; i < result.findings.length; i++)`, :380-386 per code example and per code line) and applies no cap to result.findings.length. The API-key branch of the route charges checkApiKeyRateLimit at :98-101, but the session-cookie branch starting at :111 has no limiter of any kind -- the file contains no import of lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit. Before the PDF is built, the handler also loads the full findings JSONB and runs attachRemediation over it (:150-156). The same route serves format=compliance and format=md through the same unlimited synchronous path.
impact: A signed-in user can loop the export of their own largest scan (a 250-page elite crawl merges findings across every page) and pin the single Node process's event loop in synchronous PDF construction, stalling every other user's requests and every in-flight scan's progress writes. There is no cost to the attacker and no server-side signal beyond CPU.
recommendation: Add `checkRateLimit({ key: \`report-export:${authedUserId}\`, ...RATE_LIMITS.api })` to the session branch of app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts, and cap the findings passed into generatePdfReport (e.g. the first N by severity, with a footer noting the truncation) so a single export cannot be made arbitrarily expensive.

title: Bulk scan and authenticated scan never take a concurrency slot, so the per-plan concurrentScans cap does not apply to them
description: Grepping checkConcurrentScanLimit / reserveConcurrentScanSlot across the repo returns hits only in app/api/v3/scan/route.ts (:223, :363) and app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts (:191, :435). app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts and app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts call neither. Bulk compounds this: its INSERT at :278-279 writes the completed row in one statement with no 'pending'/'running' phase (the comment at :325 says so explicitly), so a bulk scan is invisible to the counting query in lib/rate-limiting/concurrent-scans.ts:60-63 even while it is running. Bulk is bounded only by RATE_LIMITS.bulkScan (CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_BULK_SCAN_REQUESTS = 10 per hour, lib/config/config-values.ts:472-473) and runs its URL list inline and sequentially inside the request; ten concurrent bulk requests therefore run ten scan chains at once for a free user whose concurrentScans is 1 (lib/billing/catalog.ts:127). scan/authenticated is bounded by RATE_LIMITS.scan (100/hour) and its own daily-quota charge at :356.
impact: The concurrency cap that lib/rate-limiting/concurrent-scans.ts describes as the process's real capacity limit is enforced on two of the four scan entry points. A single free user can hold ten simultaneous inline bulk scan chains, each doing full outbound check batteries, against a nominal cap of one -- and the tracking table shows zero running scans the whole time, so an operator watching concurrency has no visibility into the load.
recommendation: Wrap the per-URL work in app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts and the scan in app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts in reserveConcurrentScanSlot the way app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:363 does, or -- since bulk deliberately writes terminal rows -- add a lightweight per-user in-flight counter (an advisory-lock-guarded row, mirroring reserveConcurrentScanSlot) that both routes acquire and release, so all four entry points share one capacity budget.

title: An account created through Google/GitHub/Discord can never enable 2FA: every enrollment path demands a password the account does not have
description: createOAuthUser (lib/auth/auth.ts:295 and :320) inserts `password_hash = NULL`, and verifyPassword returns false on a null hash by design (lib/auth/password-hash.ts:81). Both 2FA enrollment endpoints unconditionally require and verify a current password against that null hash. app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:109-123 rejects an empty `currentPassword` with 400 and then 403s on `!(await verifyPassword(currentPassword, pwRow.rows[0].password_hash))` -- always false for these accounts. app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-setup/route.ts:250-259 does the same (`if (!password) return badRequest; const valid = await verifyPassword(password, rows[0].password_hash); if (!valid) return forbidden`). The client makes it worse: components/profile/tabs/profile-security-tab.tsx already knows `const hasPassword = user?.hasPassword ?? true` (line 335) and uses it to reshape the password form, but the 2FA card is rendered unconditionally and the enrollment button is `disabled={totpVerifyCode.length !== 6 || !setup2FAPassword || verifying2FA}` (line 1164), so an OAuth-only user is shown the QR code, scans it, and then cannot submit at all -- the Verify button never enables. app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:116-122 documents exactly this null-hash case and deliberately skips re-auth for it, so the codebase already has the intended rule; the 2FA routes just do not follow it. app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:178 and /2fa/disable/route.ts:51 have the same blocker.
impact: Every user who signed up with Google, GitHub, or Discord is locked out of two-factor authentication on a security product, with a UI that shows the feature as available and then dead-ends. They also cannot regenerate backup codes or disable 2FA. The only workaround is to notice the separate 'Set a password' form, set one, and come back -- which nothing in the 2FA card tells them. It also means ENFORCE_STAFF_2FA (lib/auth/authorization.ts:35) permanently locks any OAuth-created staff account out of every requireStaff/requireAdmin route, with no way to satisfy the gate.
recommendation: Apply the same `hasPassword` rule app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:94-122 already uses. In app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts POST, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-setup/route.ts POST and DELETE, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/disable/route.ts, and app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts POST: read `password_hash`, and when it is null skip the currentPassword requirement entirely (the signed-in session is the re-auth signal for an account with no password), keeping the existing rate-limit buckets in place. In components/profile/tabs/profile-security-tab.tsx, hide the 'Confirm your password' input and drop `!setup2FAPassword` from the submit-disabled expression when `hasPassword` is false.

title: Five failed logins from a single IP lock any known account out for the rest of the window, and the lock is renewable forever
description: app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:95-105 gates every login on `peekRateLimit({ key: `login-fail:${user.id}`, ...RATE_LIMITS.login })` and returns 429 'Too many failed attempts for this account' when the bucket is full. The bucket is filled by the wrong-password branch at line 117 with `checkRateLimit({ key: `login-fail:${user.id}` })`, keyed by account only, accumulating across all IPs -- which is the point, but the cap is the same 5-attempt bucket as the per-IP limit (CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS = 5, CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_WINDOW_MINUTES = 15, lib/config/config-values.ts:457-458). One attacker IP is allowed exactly 5 requests per window by the `login:${ip}` gate at line 67, and 5 wrong-password requests are exactly enough to fill the account bucket to 5. peekRateLimit rejects at `count >= maxAttempts` (lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:215). Buckets are fixed windows quantized to `floor(epoch_ms / windowMs) * windowMs` (line 128), so the attacker fires 5 requests at the top of each 15-minute bucket -- 480 requests a day -- and the victim is locked continuously. A successful login never resets `login-fail:${user.id}`, and there is no unlock-by-email path anywhere; the victim is refused even with the correct password and a valid 2FA code.
impact: Anyone who knows a user's email address can keep that user permanently signed out of VulnRadar for the cost of 20 HTTP requests an hour, from a single IP, with no account of their own. Scheduled scans keep running but the owner cannot reach the dashboard, the history, or the API-key page to react. For a staff or admin account the same trick locks an operator out of the admin panel during an incident.
recommendation: Decouple the per-account cap from the per-IP cap in app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts. Give `login-fail:${user.id}` its own, much higher threshold (e.g. 25-50 over a rolling hour) so that filling it requires a genuine distributed attempt rather than one IP's normal allowance, and clear it on a successful password verify (`resetRateLimit(`login-fail:${user.id}`)` after line 107). Better still, key the account bucket on `(user.id, ip-prefix)` pairs seen and only escalate to a full account lock once several distinct source networks have failed, so a single attacker IP can never take the account down.

title: Session tokens are stored raw in the database: sessions.id IS the cookie value, unlike every other token in the codebase
category: secret stored in plaintext at rest
description: createSession generates 32 CSPRNG bytes (lib/auth/auth.ts:32-34), inserts them verbatim as the primary key at line 57 (`INSERT INTO sessions (id, ...) VALUES ($1, ...)`), and sets that same string as the cookie value at line 63. getSession looks it up with `WHERE s.id = $1` on the raw cookie (line 93). The file's own hashSessionId comment (lines 379-390) states the situation plainly: 'The `id` column is not a surrogate key: it is the literal bearer token stored in the httpOnly session cookie'. Every other bearer secret in this codebase is hashed before storage precisely so a database read cannot be replayed: password-reset tokens (app/api/v3/auth/forgot-password/route.ts:19,87), email-verification tokens (lib/auth/email-verification.ts:31), staff-invite tokens (app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:34), share tokens (AUDIT-004#secrets-01), and email 2FA codes, which even get a per-row salt (app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:222). API keys and TOTP seeds are at least AES-256-GCM encrypted (lib/auth/crypto.ts). Sessions are the only credential left in plaintext, and they are the highest-value one: lib/auth/impersonation.ts:103 also writes a second raw session id into the `imp_return_session` cookie.
impact: Any read of the sessions table -- a leaked backup, a read replica, a blind SQL injection anywhere in 155 API routes, or a support engineer with psql -- yields directly replayable, ready-to-use session cookies for every signed-in user, including admins, for up to SESSION_TIMEOUT_DAYS (7). No further work is needed by the attacker: paste the value into a `vulnradar_session` cookie. Every other token class in the app is already immune to exactly this, so the exposure is concentrated entirely in the one place it hurts most.
recommendation: Store `sha256(token)` as sessions.id and keep the raw value only in the cookie. In lib/auth/auth.ts: hash in createSession before the INSERT (line 57) and return the raw token; hash the cookie value in getSession before the SELECT (line 93) and in destroySession (line 240); hashSessionId already exists and can be reused as the digest function. The three other places that compare a raw cookie to a stored id need the same treatment: listUserSessions/findUserSessionByHash (lines 415-450, which currently hash the stored value a second time), app/api/v3/auth/sessions/route.ts:57's `s.id === currentSessionId`, and lib/auth/impersonation.ts:66-72 and :113-128. Ship it with a migration that truncates the sessions table (a forced re-login) rather than trying to convert rows in place.

title: Creating an API key requires no re-authentication, so a stolen session mints a credential that outlives 'sign out everywhere'
description: POST /api/v3/keys (app/api/v3/keys/route.ts:32) checks only `getSession()` and a plan limit before calling generateApiKey (lib/api/api-keys.ts:65), which returns the raw `vr_live_...` key in the response body. There is no current-password check and no rate limit on the endpoint. Every other sensitive action in this codebase does gate on re-auth: email and password change (app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:70-115, with its own strict `profile-reauth` login bucket), enabling TOTP (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:107-123), enabling/disabling email 2FA (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-setup/route.ts:258, :325), disabling 2FA (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/disable/route.ts:51), regenerating backup codes (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:178), and deleting the account (app/api/v3/account/delete/route.ts:70). The API key is the one credential of the set that is not merely long-lived but independent of the session that created it: DELETE /api/v3/auth/sessions (app/api/v3/auth/sessions/route.ts:62) deletes every sessions row and does not touch api_keys, and neither does a password change (app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:343-350 clears sessions and device_trust only).
impact: An attacker holding a session cookie for a few seconds -- an unlocked shared machine, a session lifted from a backup per auth-07, a support handoff -- creates an API key, reads it out of the JSON response, and keeps full scan/history/delete access on that account indefinitely. Every recovery action the victim knows about (sign out everywhere, change password, rotate 2FA) leaves the key working, and the only signal is one 'API key created' email that a user who did not create it is likely to dismiss. The key is also silently upgraded to the plan's real daily quota (line 93), so the cost lands on the victim.
recommendation: Gate POST /api/v3/keys the same way app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:75-115 gates a sensitive change: require `currentPassword` in the body, verify it against `users.password_hash` behind a `keys-create:${userId}:${ip}` bucket using RATE_LIMITS.login, and skip only the password check (never the rate limit) for the null-hash OAuth-only case. Wire the field into the create-key modal in components/profile/tabs/developer/. Separately, add `UPDATE api_keys SET revoked_at = NOW() WHERE user_id = $1` to the DELETE /api/v3/auth/sessions handler, or at minimum surface active keys on that confirmation screen, so 'sign out everywhere' means what users think it means.

title: images.unoptimized is on and Discord sign-in avatars are stored without a ?size= parameter, so 1024px PNGs are downloaded to fill 14px circles on /public-scans
description: next.config.mjs:25-27 sets `images: { unoptimized: true }`, which turns every next/image into a pass-through with no resizing and no format negotiation. lib/auth/oauth-userinfo.ts:231 builds the Discord sign-in avatar URL as `https://cdn.discordapp.com/avatars/${data.id}/${data.avatar}.png` with no size query parameter, so Discord's CDN serves the full-resolution PNG (the same file elsewhere in the codebase is requested with an explicit cap: components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:636 uses ?size=128 and app/api/v3/account/discord/route.ts:181 uses ?size=256). GitHub avatars at lib/auth/oauth-userinfo.ts:203 store the raw avatar_url, which githubusercontent serves at its default resolution. Those stored URLs are then rendered at thumbnail size: components/public-scans/public-scan-row.tsx:80 renders `` for every row of the public scans directory, and components/admin/shared/user-avatar.tsx:32 renders width={48} into `h-7 w-7` (28px) rows. Locally uploaded avatars are unaffected -- components/modals/image-crop-dialog.tsx:167 crops them to 256px before upload -- so this is specifically the OAuth-provider path.
impact: A page of the public scans directory can pull one full-resolution provider avatar per row to render 14x14 thumbnails. A Discord PNG at default resolution is commonly a few hundred kilobytes, so a 20-row listing can transfer several megabytes of avatar data for roughly 4 KB of rendered pixels, on a page anonymous visitors and crawlers hit.
recommendation: Append a size cap where the URL is built: change lib/auth/oauth-userinfo.ts:231 to `...png?size=128` (matching the connect flow at app/api/v3/account/discord/route.ts:181) and lib/auth/oauth-userinfo.ts:203 to append `&s=128` to the GitHub avatar_url. Separately, reconsider `images: { unoptimized: true }` in next.config.mjs:26 -- sharp is already pinned in the package.json overrides, so enabling the optimizer with remotePatterns for the three provider CDNs would fix the existing stored URLs too.

title: Bulk scan charges a daily-quota slot per URL before that URL is SSRF/access-rule validated, so blocked URLs permanently burn quota for work never done
description: The bulk loop calls `const dailyQuota = await checkAndRecordRequest(authedUserId!)` at app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts:637 -- an atomic check-AND-increment, so the slot is consumed at that moment -- and only afterwards calls runSingleScan at line 688. runSingleScan is where the URL is actually validated: validateScanTarget at line 104 (SSRF / private-address rejection) and checkAccessRules at line 114 (blacklist). Both return `{ success: false, error }` without ever running a scan, and there is no refund, no decrement, and no compensating call anywhere in the file. POST /api/v3/scan deliberately fixed this exact ordering and documents it at app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:196-200 ("Charging up front used to burn a scan from the daily allowance for requests that were then rejected (concurrency 429, an invalid/SSRF-blocked URL, an unverified domain) with no refund path") by moving the charge to :397, after validation and slot reservation; POST /api/v3/scan/authenticated does the same at :356. Bulk is the remaining outlier. This is a live instance of the prior 'M1 quota-charge-before-validation' backlog item (AUDIT full-audit 2026-08-25 notes).
impact: A user who submits a batch containing internal, private, or blacklisted hosts (http://localhost, http://192.168.1.1, 169.254.169.254, any admin-blacklisted domain) has one daily scan deducted for each of them even though nothing was scanned. On the Free plan (25/day) a single 25-URL batch of blocked targets zeroes the account's entire day with zero scans performed, and there is no way to get it back before midnight UTC. This is self-inflicted rather than cross-tenant, but it is a support-ticket generator and it makes the used/limit numbers reported by GET /api/v3/billing describe work that never happened.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts, hoist runSingleScan's two gates -- validateScanTarget (currently line 104) and checkAccessRules (line 114) -- out of runSingleScan and into the loop body ahead of the checkAndRecordRequest call at line 637, pushing the rejection result and `continue`-ing without charging. Alternatively split runSingleScan into a validate step and an execute step and only call checkAndRecordRequest between them. Either shape matches the ordering POST /api/v3/scan already documents.

title: Raw exception messages from the scan pipeline are persisted into scan_history.error_message and rendered verbatim to the user with a Copy button
description: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:1112-1118 takes any non-cancellation throw from the whole scan pipeline and does `const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : ...; await finalizeScanFailure(scanId, message)`. lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:830-833 is identical. app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:430-433 does the same for a dispatch-time throw. finalizeScanFailure (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:364-380) writes that string straight into `scan_history.error_message`. GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id] then returns it unmodified: `responseBody.error = row.error_message ?? "The scan failed."` (app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts:219). The dashboard renders it as-is in a monospace block at components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:257-259, next to a "Copy error details" button (:235) that copies it to the clipboard. Nothing between the throw and the screen sanitizes the string, so a pg driver message (`relation "scan_tags" does not exist`, `connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.5:5432`), a Node DNS error naming an internal host, or an unexpected library stack message reaches the end user and is retained in the scan row. This is the same class AUDIT-011#brow-01 filed for the browser-session viewer, on a much higher-traffic path.
impact: A user hitting an internal server problem sees the server's own infrastructure details (internal hostnames, private IPs, table and column names) presented as their scan result, and the string is persisted in scan_history for the retention period. It also makes the error UI's classifyError (dashboard-error-state.tsx:44-80) misfire, since it substring-matches on words like "invalid" and "private" that appear in driver text for unrelated reasons.
recommendation: In lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:1113 and lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:831, keep the raw message in the existing console.error and pass a mapped, fixed reason to finalizeScanFailure (a small enum: target unreachable / target blocked / scan timed out / internal error, plus the scan id). Same for app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:431. That keeps app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts:219 safe without changing its shape.

title: GET /api/v3/auth/me issues seven queries per call, reading the same users row three times and gifted_subscriptions twice, and it runs on every page load
category: redundant queries on the hottest authenticated route
description: `getSession()` at app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts:61 already runs `SELECT ... FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON s.user_id = u.id WHERE s.id = $1` (lib/auth/auth.ts:98-104). The route then runs a six-way `Promise.all` at line 79 which reads the same users row again (lines 80-88), reads `gifted_subscriptions` (lines 96-99), and calls `getUserPlanLimits(session.userId)` (line 110) which calls `getUserPlan` (lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:75) -- a third read of the users row joined against gifted_subscriptions a second time. Net: 7 queries, 6 of them concurrent out of a pool whose max is 10 (lib/config/config-values.ts:393), for data that is one users row, one badges join, and one discord row.
impact: This is the endpoint `AuthProvider` calls on every page navigation, so it is the highest-frequency authenticated query in the product. Every page view costs 7 database round trips instead of 3, and two simultaneous page loads from different users take 12-14 of the 10 available pool connections, forcing everything else in the process to queue.
recommendation: Have `getSession` return (or a request-scoped cache hold) the users row so lines 80-88 do not re-read it, and pass the already-fetched plan into `getUserPlanLimits` instead of letting it call `getUserPlan` again. Fold the `gifted_subscriptions` lookup into the single users query with a LEFT JOIN, exactly as `getUserPlan` already does. That takes the route from 7 queries to 3.

title: An invalid API key falls through to a full scan of the legacy key rows and a bcryptjs comparison per row, on the main thread
category: unbounded work on an unauthenticated failure path
description: `validateApiKey` tries the O(1) locator lookup first (lib/api/api-keys.ts:336), but when it matches nothing it does not return. It then runs `SELECT ... WHERE ak.key_locator IS NULL AND ak.key_encrypted IS NOT NULL` (line 362) and AES-decrypts every returned row, and then `SELECT ... WHERE ak.key_hash IS NOT NULL AND ak.key_locator IS NULL AND ak.key_encrypted IS NULL` (line 392) and calls `verifyKey(key, row.key_hash)` for every row in a `for` loop (line 404). `verifyKey` is `bcrypt.compare` from `bcryptjs` (lines 2 and 126) -- the pure-JavaScript implementation, which does its work on the main thread rather than the libuv pool -- against hashes generated at cost 12 (`const saltRounds = 12`, line 120). Only on a match is the locator backfilled (line 376), so a legacy key that is never used again keeps its row in the scanned set forever.
impact: Every request with a wrong, revoked or stale Bearer token costs three extra queries and one main-thread bcrypt-12 comparison per un-backfilled legacy row. bcryptjs at cost 12 is on the order of 200-400ms of JavaScript CPU per comparison, so a handful of legacy rows turns each bad token into a second or more of event-loop time in a single-process deployment -- and POST /api/v3/scan reaches this before any rate limiting applies (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:65).
recommendation: In lib/api/api-keys.ts:326, return `null` immediately after the locator lookup misses unless a one-time startup check confirms un-backfilled rows still exist (`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM api_keys WHERE key_locator IS NULL)`, cached in module scope and cleared on key creation). Run the backfill as a migration in instrumentation.ts rather than lazily on match, then delete the two fallback scans entirely.

title: POST /api/v3/scan/bulk does roughly nine sequential database round trips per URL, up to 900-1000 in one request, and takes a row lock on the API key each time
description: The bulk route loops `for (let i = 0; i < urlsToScan.length; i++)` at app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts:622 with every step awaited in order. Per iteration: `checkAndRecordRequest` (line 637) costs `getDailyLimit` -> `getUserPlan` plus an UPSERT and possibly a re-read (lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:309/330/361/378) = 2-3 queries; `checkApiKeyRateLimit` (line 668) runs `pool.connect` + BEGIN + `SELECT id FROM api_keys WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` (lib/api/api-keys.ts:489) + a 24h `COUNT(*)` over api_usage (line 505) + an INSERT (line 514) + COMMIT + an `UPDATE api_keys SET last_used_at` (line 528) + a `SELECT used_at ... LIMIT 1` (line 543) = 7 round trips holding a row lock; `runSingleScan` (line 688) adds `checkAccessRules` (2 queries) and an `INSERT INTO scan_history`. `MAX_URLS_BULK` defaults to 100 (lib/config/config-values.ts:543).
impact: A 100-URL bulk request performs on the order of 900-1000 serialized database round trips inside one HTTP handler, acquiring and releasing a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the same api_keys row 100 times, while holding pool connections throughout. Even at 2ms RTT that is two seconds of pure database latency layered on top of 100 sequential network scans.
recommendation: Hoist the per-user work out of the loop in app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts:622: resolve the plan and daily limit once, charge quota for the whole batch in one capped statement, and record API usage once per batch (or as a single multi-row INSERT at the end) rather than per URL. Cache the access-rules result per host for the duration of the request.

title: Four routes select the full findings JSONB for an unbounded row set, including a GDPR export that buffers the entire admin audit log into memory twice
description: (a) app/api/v3/shares/route.ts:15-30 selects `summary, findings` for every share a user owns with no LIMIT, then JSON.parses each blob in JS at lines 32-36 -- and the only derived value is `findingsCount: findings.length` (line 50), which the `findings_count` column already stores. (b) app/api/v3/admin/audit-log/export/route.ts:79-88 runs `SELECT ... FROM admin_audit_log al LEFT JOIN users au ... LEFT JOIN users tu ... ORDER BY al.created_at DESC` with no WHERE and no LIMIT, buffers all rows into a JS array (line 81) and then `JSON.stringify(result.rows, null, 2)` (line 104) -- the entire audit table held in the Node heap twice. (c) lib/notifications/posture-digest.ts:80-93 runs `SELECT DISTINCT ON (url) url, findings FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 AND status = 'completed' ORDER BY url, scanned_at DESC` with no LIMIT and no time bound, and it is called twice per user at lines 113-117. (d) app/api/v3/data-request/route.ts:167-174 selects `findings` for every scan the user ever ran.
impact: (b) is the sharpest: an admin clicking Export on a mature instance OOM-kills the single Node process that also runs every in-flight scan, since `admin_audit_log` grows on every staff action and there is no bound at all.
