(a) and (d) ship tens of megabytes per request for users with many scans. (c) makes the digest worker's cost scale with total history rather than with what the digest actually reports.
recommendation: Add `findings_count` to (a) and drop `findings` from the projection entirely. Stream (b) with a keyset-paged cursor and write CSV/NDJSON incrementally instead of building one string, and bound it with the same retention window lib/database/audit-log-archive.ts:80 uses. Give (c) a `LIMIT` and a `scanned_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '...'` bound, and project only the finding fields the digest renders. Page (d) or stream it to a file.

title: Single requests fan out more concurrent queries than the entire connection pool holds: 25 from the data-export route against a pool max of 10
description: `CONFIG_DB_POOL_MAX` is 10 (lib/config/config-values.ts:393), wired into the Pool at lib/database/db.ts:58. app/api/v3/data-request/route.ts:97-122 destructures 25 results from a single `Promise.all` at line 123, each of them a `pool.query` -- so one request asks for 25 connections at once and queues on itself for 15 of them, several of which are unbounded (sessions at :137-143, api_usage joined to api_keys at :155-164, all of scan_history with findings at :167-174, scan_tags at :178-183). app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:146 fans out exactly 10 in the `user-detail` branch, monopolizing the pool. app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:33 fans out 7 (perf-06), and app/api/v3/admin/billing-overview/route.ts:103 fans out 7 including three full `users` counts. Separately, lib/database/cleanup.ts:481-498 fires `2 x N` unawaited `.catch()`ed writes for expired browser sessions with no cap.
impact: Any one of these requests can starve every other request in the process -- including `getSession`, so an admin opening a user detail page can make other users' logins hang until `connectionTimeoutMillis` fires. The pool is a process-wide resource and nothing in the codebase budgets it per request.
recommendation: Cap fan-out per request. Either raise `CONFIG_DB_POOL_MAX` well above the largest fan-out and size Postgres accordingly, or (better) batch: the data-export route's 25 queries are mostly `WHERE user_id = $1` on different tables and can run in chunks of 4-5, and the admin user-detail branch can be consolidated into 2-3 joined queries. Add an explicit concurrency limiter to the cleanup fan-out at lib/database/cleanup.ts:481.

title: The authenticated-scan endpoint will POST caller-supplied credentials to any public host, so it works as a credential-validation proxy against sites the caller does not own
description:
POST /api/v3/scan/authenticated accepts a target `url` plus an `auth` object carrying a username and password (app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:298-303) and hands both to establishScanSession at :334. That walks to lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts:456-489, which builds `username=<caller value>&password=<caller value>` plus the target's own hidden fields and POSTs it to the discovered form action via safeFetch with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `Referer`, `Origin` and an `X-CSRF-Token` scraped from the page. The only host restriction is `allowedHostnames: [hostnameOf(origin)]`: the caller's own chosen origin.

The domain-ownership gate at app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:312-330 fires only when `requestsActiveProbing(scanners)` is true. A plain authenticated scan of a domain the caller has never verified is explicitly allowed. The outcome is reported back distinguishably: lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts:496-498 returns "The target rejected the login request with 401", :505-509 returns "The login did not set or change any cookie", :511-515 returns "still showed a login form", and success returns a completed scan: the route surfaces the reason verbatim at app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:341-346. That is a clean three-way oracle for whether a credential pair is valid on a third-party site.

The only limits are checkGlobalRateLimit on `scan-authenticated:<userId>` (:200-207) and the per-account daily scan quota (:189, :208-215). Signup is free and open, so both scale with the number of accounts an attacker creates.
impact: VulnRadar's server IP becomes the origin of credential-stuffing attempts against arbitrary third-party login forms, with a built-in success oracle and CSRF-token handling already done for the attacker. The victim site's logs, lockouts and abuse reports point at VulnRadar, which for a service with a public reputation and a shared egress IP means blocklisting and abuse complaints. It also puts the operator in the position of having proxied unauthorised authentication attempts.
recommendation: Apply the same ownership gate to the credential-submitting path that active-probes already has. In app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts, move the `isUrlOwnedByUser(url, authedUserId)` check at :312-330 out of the `requestsActiveProbing(scanners)` condition and require it whenever `parsed.data.auth` carries a username/password (form or basic auth); a cookie-only session (`auth.cookies`, lib/scanner/auth/login.ts:86) is the caller supplying their own already-established session and can stay ungated. Keep a per-target-host failure counter so repeated 401s against one host stop the feature for that account regardless of quota.

title: The bulk remediation endpoint fans out 200 unbatched queries with no transaction, making its error message dishonest
description: app/api/v3/scan/remediation/bulk/route.ts:83-119 issues Promise.all over up to 200 independent pool.query calls with no transaction. Partial failure leaves partial state while the UI shows a generic 'Couldn't apply. Try again.' Separately lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:366 declares security: [{ apiKey: [] }] for this route (and :337 for the single route) but neither handler has a Bearer path, so an API-key client following the published spec gets a 401.
impact: A user who retries after a partial failure re-applies to findings already changed, and cannot tell which ones took. The endpoint has zero external consumers because the published spec is wrong about its auth.
recommendation: Replace the fan-out with one INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM unnest(...) inside a transaction, then the all-or-nothing error copy becomes true. Correct or remove the apiKey security declaration in the OpenAPI spec. Note this is a prerequisite for the undo described in bulk-01.

title: Fifteen permission constants gate nothing, including two for a reports feature that does not exist
description: Dead constants in lib/auth/permissions-client.ts: VIEW_USER_API_KEYS (:29), DELETE_ANY_TEAM (:76), VIEW_REPORTS (:80) and RESOLVE_REPORTS (:81) - there is no reports feature or table at all - VIEW_DEBUG_INFO (:92), CLEAR_CACHE (:94), SEND_USER_EMAILS (:85), ACCESS_ADMIN_PANEL (:11), ACCESS_STAFF_PAGE (:12) granted to six roles while app/staff does not exist, VIEW_USER_SESSIONS (:27), VIEW_BADGES (:34), VIEW_ALL_SCANS (:41), VIEW_SCAN_STATS (:43), VIEW_SUBSCRIPTIONS (:47), MANAGE_SUBSCRIPTIONS (:48). requireModerator() at lib/auth/authorization.ts:102-122 has zero call sites. Separately, several cards render ungated where a permission exists for them: the API Keys card at user-detail-panel.tsx:2561, sessions at :2667, all-scans at :2507, and badges at admin/route.ts:281-286 which has no permission call unlike its neighbours at :249 and :294.
impact: An operator granting or withholding these permissions changes nothing, which is a security-adjacent false assurance. The ungated cards are the mirror image: data visible to staff roles that were never granted access to it.
recommendation: Split into two passes: wire the four ungated cards to their existing permissions first, since that is a real access-control gap; then delete or implement the fifteen dead constants.

title: Four backend capabilities are gated behind conditions nothing can satisfy
description: domains.team_id (instrumentation.ts:3176) is read for team access at app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:33, but the INSERT at :120 omits it, no PATCH exists anywhere under app/api/v3/domains/ (exports are GET, POST, DELETE plus verify POST), all four UPDATE/INSERT statements skip it, and components/profile/tabs/domains-section.tsx:147 hardcodes team_id: null - yet app/docs/teams/page.tsx:425 documents it as a feature. DEFAULT_API_KEY_DAILY_LIMIT (registry.ts:1527-1536) is admin-editable and read at lib/api/api-keys.ts:70 via `dailyLimit ?? await getSetting(...)`, but generateApiKey has exactly one production caller (app/api/v3/keys/route.ts:95) which always passes an explicit number, so the branch is dead; compounding, app/docs/api/page.tsx:738 and app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:173 tell users the default is 50 while the real value is the plan's apiRequestsPerDay, 25 on Free. access_rules.is_active = false is writable via the API but the list query filters WHERE is_active = true (admin/features/route.ts:168), so a deactivated rule vanishes and can never be reactivated. The empty-string state of CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and FIREFOX_ADDON_URL (registry.ts:397-412) is documented as falling back to a packaged release, but the admin write goes through z.url() which rejects "", the env path skips empty overrides (runtime-config.ts:89), and reset restores a non-empty default - and the fallback UI does not exist either, since app/docs/extension/page.tsx:113,139 link unconditionally under a hardcoded 'Live' badge.
impact: Four documented behaviours that cannot occur. The API key limit case additionally publishes a wrong number to users in two docs pages.
recommendation: Correct the two docs pages about the API key default immediately, since that is user-facing misinformation. Then either implement domains.team_id (a PATCH route plus a selector) or remove it and its docs claim.

title: Two entitlements are enforced but never advertised, and one has no admin setting at all
description: The crawl page-selection limit is hardcoded at lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:18-23 (25/50/100/250) and enforced at app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:258, but a grep for CRAWL_PAGES in lib/config/registry.ts returns zero. It is the only per-plan entitlement with no registry key, so it is absent from Admin > Settings > Billing and from components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx, surfacing only at point of use (components/scanner/crawl-url-selector.tsx:50). githubReviewTokensPerWindow is enforced per plan but no plan's features array mentions GitHub review (only AI review tokens at lib/billing/catalog.ts:141,174,205), so a Free user hits a hard 403 with no prior signal. Separately, lib/billing/github-review-usage.ts:365-372 implements a free-plan trial whose own comment reads 'Hidden trial, never advertised on the pricing page', while Free's githubReviewTokensPerWindow of 0 makes components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:85-89 render a cross for Free.
impact: Two invisible paywalls that users meet as a 403 rather than as a plan comparison, and a genuine free-tier benefit that the pricing page actively denies exists.
recommendation: Add BILLING_*_CRAWL_PAGES registry keys and a Scanning row on /pricing. Add a GitHub review row to the plan comparison. Decide whether the hidden trial should be advertised; if it stays hidden, stop rendering a cross for a capability Free actually has.

title: Stale, non-super_admin-aware role helpers still dead-exported through the @/lib/auth barrel
description: lib/auth/permissions.ts defines canManageRole/canAccessAdmin/getRoleLevel/isStaffRole against an old ROLES map with no super_admin. lib/auth/permissions-client.ts has newer versions built on STAFF_ROLE_HIERARCHY which does include super_admin. lib/auth/index.ts re-exports the OLD versions as the public @/lib/auth API. Currently unreachable in practice (the one real caller bypasses the barrel) but any future import from @/lib/auth silently gets the version that mishandles a super_admin.
recommendation: Have permissions.ts re-export the client versions instead of redefining them, or delete the local duplicates.

title: Host-level reputation lookup echoes the exact scanned URL (with query string) of an unrelated public scan to any signed-in user
description: GET /api/v3/scan/reputation falls back to the host-level host_reputation row when no exact-URL match is found, and returns that row's scanned_url column verbatim -- the literal URL, including query string, of whatever page on that host was most recently scanned publicly by anyone, not necessarily the page the caller asked about. Any signed-in account can query a bare host and learn the exact URL of a different, unrelated page someone else scanned. Since scan_history.is_public defaults to true, if that URL embedded a secret in its query string (password-reset link, magic-login link, API token) the secret becomes readable by any account holder who only knows the hostname. The is_public privacy gate itself is correctly enforced -- the leak is specifically scanned_url being echoed on the host-level fallback, where the caller never supplied that URL themselves.
recommendation: Only return scannedUrl on an exact match (the caller already supplied, and thus already knows, that URL); return null for a host-level fallback match.

title: billing_verification_codes missing per-row salt
description: Verification codes in billing_verification_codes are hashed without a per-row salt. If the table is leaked, codes can be cracked with a rainbow table over the small (typically 6-digit numeric) code space.
recommendation: ALTER TABLE billing_verification_codes ADD COLUMN salt TEXT; generate random salt per code; store hash(salt || code); verify by re-hashing with the stored salt.
fixSummary: Migration 3.0.0-to-3.1.0.mjs adds billing_verification_codes.salt TEXT. Application code (billing-verify routes) must be updated to write random salts and verify via hash(salt+code). Column exists but write/verify logic is pending.

title: Self-account-delete has no password challenge or grace period
description: POST /api/v3/account/delete destroys the account immediately. No password re-entry, no email confirmation, no grace period.
recommendation: Require currentPassword before deletion; send confirmation email with revocation link; implement a 7-day grace period (mark disabled instead of hard-delete).

title: Signup rate-limited only by IP, not by email
description: Per-IP signup throttling only. No per-email cap. Attacker can rotate IPs to enumerate which emails are registered (409 vs success differentiates them) and DoS by flooding signup tables.
recommendation: Add per-email throttling (e.g., 5 per hour per email).

title: Share tokens stored plaintext in scan_history
description: share_token is a 64-char hex random in plaintext. A DB read yields all share URLs, granting indefinite read access to long-lived shared scans.
recommendation: Store sha256(share_token) at rest; look up by hashed value; return raw token only at creation time (already done).

title: Team invite tokens stored plaintext
description: team_invites.token is plaintext. No rate limit on accept-invite either.
recommendation: Hash tokens at rest; add per-IP rate limit on accept-invite.

title: Password reset does not clear device_trust rows
description: reset-password deletes sessions but NOT device_trust. An attacker who previously compromised the device (got the device_trust cookie planted) can still bypass 2FA on subsequent logins.
recommendation: Add DELETE FROM device_trust WHERE user_id = $1 in the same transaction as the session wipe.

title: Audit-log IPs read leftmost X-Forwarded-For (spoofable)
description: 7 routes trusted the client-supplied IP without consulting TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDR.
recommendation: Replace with await getClientIp() everywhere.

title: browser/sessions had no per-user cap (financial DoS)
description: A compromised session could rack up real BrowserBase costs by spawning unlimited sessions.
recommendation: Added RATE_LIMITS.browserSession (20/hour per user).

title: window_start at ms precision created a fresh bucket per request
description: ON CONFLICT(key, window_start) matched exact ms; attacker firing N requests in 1ms got N buckets at count=1.
recommendation: Quantize window_start to floor(epoch_ms / window_ms) * window_ms.

title: No URL length cap at scan API boundary
description: CONFIG_MAX_URL_LENGTH was defined but never enforced — a 50MB URL string hit DNS resolution and DB INSERT.
recommendation: Reject with 400 before any DNS / DB work when url.length > SCANNING.MAX_URL_LENGTH.

title: scan_history.response_headers stored Set-Cookie values
description: Scan-target session cookies persisted to DB indefinitely.
recommendation: redactSensitiveResponseHeaders strips Set-Cookie / Cookie / Authorization / etc. before insert.

title: Bulk scan limit hardcoded to 10 instead of MAX_URLS_IN_BULK (100)
description: Self-hosters configuring MAX_URLS_IN_BULK got silent bypass.
recommendation: Use SCANNING.MAX_URLS_IN_BULK.

title: admin_audit_log.details stored raw user emails (365-day retention)
description: Emails leaked in audit log long after the user changed or deleted their address.
recommendation: Central logAuditAction helper masks any email-like substring via redactEmailsInDetails before insert.

title: The shared modal hook never hides the page behind the dialog from assistive tech, despite its own comment claiming it does
description: lib/hooks/use-modal-a11y.ts is the accessibility layer for eleven hand-rolled modals. Its comment at :58-61 says the Tab trap stops a keyboard user stepping out "into the (aria-hidden) page behind it", but nothing in the file ever sets aria-hidden or inert on anything: the three effects handle Escape (:45-56), Tab containment (:62-93) and focus save/restore (:96-118), and `dialogProps` (:121-128) applies only role, aria-modal, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby and tabIndex to the panel itself. The parenthetical describes behaviour that does not exist. Radix's Dialog, which components/ui/dialog.tsx wraps, does apply aria-hidden to sibling nodes, so the hand-rolled modals behave differently from the shadcn ones in the same app.
impact: A screen-reader user in browse mode can still arrow through the whole page behind an open modal, including the ToS gate (components/modals/tos-modal.tsx:164) whose entire purpose is to block interaction until accepted. Real but bounded: aria-modal="true" causes most modern screen readers to constrain the virtual buffer anyway, so this is a belt-and-braces gap rather than an outright block.
recommendation: In lib/hooks/use-modal-a11y.ts, add an effect that sets `inert` (with an aria-hidden fallback) on the direct children of document.body other than the modal's own portal root while `open` is true, and clears it on close. Then correct the comment at :59 either way.

title: The API-key 429 on POST /scan hardcodes "50 requests per 24 hours" regardless of the key's actual limit
description: app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:123-130 returns `{ error: "Rate limit exceeded. 50 requests per 24 hours.", limit: rateLimit.limit, used, remaining, resets_at }`. The structured fields are correct, but the human-readable string is a literal 50 while the real limit is the key's daily_limit, itself set from the plan's apiRequestsPerDay (see apidoc-08): 25 on free, 100 on core, 5000 on pro, 999999 on elite. app/docs/api/page.tsx:1392-1399 documents the 429 body as carrying the true numbers, which it does, so only the message disagrees.
impact: A Pro user cut off after 5,000 requests reads that their key allows 50 and opens a support ticket; a free user cut off at 25 reads 50 and assumes a bug.
recommendation: Interpolate `rateLimit.limit` into the message at app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:125, matching the wording app/api/v3/history/route.ts:187 already uses.

title: There is no customer SSO or SAML: the only OIDC path is staff-only and by design never creates or promotes an account
description: app/api/v3/auth/staff-oidc/route.ts:1 to :4 states the posture: the OIDC flow "never creates or promotes an account; only signs into an existing staff-or-above account whose email matches the IdP's". Customer sign-in is password plus 2FA plus Google, GitHub and Discord OAuth (app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/route.ts). A grep for saml or SAML across lib/ and app/ returns nothing. Among peers, Burp Suite DAST supports SAML, Okta and Entra ID, and Intruder lists Okta SSO; the rest are not documented to.
impact: SSO is the gate on selling to a company rather than a person. With paid tiers at $5 to $20 a month and roughly 50 registered users, no prospect in that band is blocked by its absence today, and the buyers who require SAML are buying at Burp and Snyk price points with procurement processes this product is not set up for.
recommendation: Do not build this now. Record it as a deliberate deferral so it stops resurfacing in feature lists. If a team plan is ever priced above roughly $200/month, the cheapest correct path is to extend the existing lib/auth/staff-oidc.ts discovery-document machinery to a per-team issuer configuration rather than adding a SAML stack, since generic OIDC covers Okta, Entra ID and Google Workspace and reuses code that is already written and audited.

title: The password strength gate `score < 3` is repeated as an unnamed literal in five routes and one component with no shared constant and no way to tune it
description: analyzePassword returns a 0-4 style score (lib/auth/password-strength.ts:417). The cutoff that decides whether a password is accepted is written as the bare comparison `pwAnalysis.score < 3` in four server routes: app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:89, app/api/v3/auth/reset-password/route.ts:47, app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:302 and app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:171. components/auth/reset-password-form.tsx:49 repeats `analysis.score < 3` client-side to drive the advisory meter. There is no exported constant and no registry key; a grep of lib/config for a password-score setting returns only PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH. The comment at lib/auth/password-strength.ts:663 explicitly notes the score is 'useful for a strength meter, useless as' a gate on its own, yet five sites gate on it.
impact: Raising or lowering the strength bar means finding and editing five identical comparisons, and missing the client one leaves the meter green on a password the server will reject. The gate is also invisible to an operator: nothing in the admin panel or the docs states that a password can fail after passing the documented length check.
recommendation: Export a MIN_PASSWORD_SCORE constant from lib/auth/password-strength.ts, use it at all five sites, and document it next to PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH in app/docs/account-security so users understand why a 12-character password can still be refused.

title: Six user-facing list endpoints carry hard SQL LIMITs with no pagination, no total, and no client-side awareness of the cap
description: AUDIT-013#dup-15 verified that the seven properly paginated routes share one page/limit convention. These six do not participate in it and cap silently instead: app/api/v3/support-tickets/route.ts:45 (LIMIT 100 on a user's own tickets), app/api/v3/admin/support-tickets/route.ts:56 (LIMIT 200 on the staff inbox), app/api/v3/scan/remediation/route.ts:165 (LIMIT 500 on triage state), app/api/v3/teams/member-scans/route.ts:58 (LIMIT 50), app/api/v3/badge/scans/route.ts:34 (LIMIT 50) and app/api/v3/admin/blocked-data/route.ts:80 (LIMIT 100). None returns a total. Two of them then feed a client-side paginator that reports the capped array as the total: components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx:124 passes totalItems={scans.length} over the server-capped 50, and components/ui/pagination-control.tsx:11 offers page sizes of 10, 25, 50 and 100, so selecting 100 on the teammate-scans panel yields a single page that can never contain more than 50 rows. A related client blind spot: app/api/v3/scan/remediation/bulk/route.ts:31 caps the items array at 200 via zod, but components/scanner/results-list.tsx:176 sends `[...selected]` unchunked and its catch at :219-:221 sets a generic bulkError flag, so an over-cap submission fails with no explanation of the limit.
impact: A long-running account's support history, triage state and teammate activity are truncated with no indication, and the paginator actively asserts the truncated count is the total. On the staff inbox the 200-row cap means an older open ticket can drop off the only list staff have.
recommendation: Adopt the page/limit convention AUDIT-013#dup-15 documented for these six routes, returning a total alongside the rows, and pass that total into PaginationControl instead of array length. For the bulk remediation cap, export the 200 as a shared constant and have components/scanner/results-list.tsx chunk at it rather than relying on a server rejection.

title: Every daily-activity tooltip on the dashboard reports 0 issues, because the API hardcodes the field it renders
description:
The dashboard's 14-day activity strip renders a tooltip per bar at components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:320-328, whose second line is `{d.scans} scans` followed by, when `d.scans > 0`, ` · ${d.issues} issues` (:324-325). `issues` comes from the API's dailyActivity mapping at app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:99-105, which builds each row as `{ day: row.day, scans: Number(row.scans) || 0, issues: 0 }`. The literal 0 at :102 is the only value that field ever takes; the underlying query at :63-77 selects only day and a scan count and never touches findings. The client's own normalisation at dashboard.tsx:244-248 preserves it as 0.

So every tooltip on a day with any activity reads `3 scans · 0 issues`, on an account whose Findings by severity panel two hundred pixels below shows hundreds of findings.
impact: The tooltip states, for every active day, that the scans that day found nothing. It contradicts the rest of the page and it is the only per-day findings figure the product offers, so a user checking whether a bad week was actually bad is told no.
recommendation: Either populate it or remove it. To populate: extend the weekly-activity query at app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:63-77 to also sum findings_count per day, `COALESCE(SUM(sh.findings_count), 0)::int as issues`, and pass `Number(row.issues) || 0` through the mapping at :102 instead of the literal. To remove: delete the `issues` field from the mapping and delete the conditional clause at components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:324-325. Populating is the better answer, since a per-day findings figure is one of the few things on that page that answers what changed since I was last here.

title: /alternatives/intelliradar is a comparison page that compares nothing: three of its five table rows say "Varies by product." and its summary describes the category rather than the competitor
description: lib/seo/alternatives.ts:55 defines the `intelliradar` entry, one of five in ALTERNATIVES and therefore one of five sitemap entries at priority 0.6 (lib/seo/routes.ts:72). Its `summary` (line 57) is category-level, not product-level: "IntelliRadar is a security scanning tool in the same broad space as VulnRadar: point it at a target and get back a list of findings. Products in this category differ mostly in what they inspect, how they price, and whether you can run them yourself." Its five ComparisonRow entries put "Varies by product." in the competitor column three times (lines 71, 81, 86), "Check the vendor's site; openness varies by product." once, and "See the vendor's current pricing." once. Its `positioning` opens "If you found VulnRadar while searching for IntelliRadar...". The other four entries (detectify, intruder, probely, qualys) all carry real, specific, factual competitor descriptions, so this is a single outlier in an otherwise well-built cluster. The file's own header comment at lines 1-13 sets the rule the entry breaks: "Competitor pricing is NEVER invented" is honoured, but so is every other fact, leaving the page empty.
impact: A page whose entire competitor column is "Varies by product" is a doorway page for a brand name with no content behind it. In a five-page cluster, one page like this pulls down the perceived quality of the other four, which are genuinely good comparison pages that could rank for "detectify alternative" and "probely alternative". It also fails a human reader instantly, so anyone who does land on it bounces.
recommendation: Either fill it or drop it. Filling it means the same treatment as the detectify entry: a specific description of what IntelliRadar actually is, and real values in the five rows. Dropping it means removing the entry from ALTERNATIVES in lib/seo/alternatives.ts:54-104, which automatically removes the sitemap entry (lib/seo/routes.ts:72 derives from getAllAlternatives()) and leaves a clean four-page cluster. Given the comparison-set gap analysis in section 20, the higher-value move is to spend the same effort adding entries for the open-source self-hostable comparisons (OWASP ZAP, Nuclei) and the single-URL free scanners (Mozilla Observatory, Security Headers, SSL Labs), which are the tools this product is genuinely searched against.

title: A no-op ternary in the Discord OAuth callback collapses a state/session mismatch into the same error code as a forged state, so the replay case the HMAC binding exists to catch is invisible
description: app/api/v3/auth/discord/callback/route.ts:83-88 reads: const reason = verified.reason === 'expired' ? 'discord_expired' : verified.reason === 'user-mismatch' ? 'discord_invalid_state' : 'discord_invalid_state'. Both arms of the second ternary are the string 'discord_invalid_state', so the 'user-mismatch' test on line 86 can never change the result and is dead. verifyDiscordState (lib/auth/discord-state.ts:75) returns four distinct reasons: 'malformed' (lines 79, 100, 109), 'bad-signature' (88, 91, 94), 'expired' (112, 121) and 'user-mismatch' (128). The user-mismatch branch is the one that fires when a validly signed state is presented by a different session than it was issued to, which is exactly the leaked-state-replay case the HMAC binding at line 81 was added to detect. It is reported to the user, and to anyone reading logs by error code, as an ordinary invalid state. This is a second instance of the class already filed as AUDIT-011#docs-06 (components/docs/docs-nav.ts:153, 'item.exact ? pathname === item.href : pathname === item.href'); I scanned every .ts/.tsx/.mjs file outside node_modules and tests for ternaries with textually identical arms and these two are the only ones in the tree.
impact: A user whose Discord link attempt is rejected because the state belongs to a different session sees the same generic message as someone whose state was truncated by an email client, so support cannot tell a benign copy-paste from an attempted state replay. The code reads as though the two cases are distinguished, which is worse than not branching at all.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/auth/discord/callback/route.ts:83-88, give the user-mismatch arm its own code, e.g. 'discord_state_session_mismatch', and add a matching message on the login page, or delete lines 86-87 and keep a flat expired/other split. Whichever is chosen, log verified.reason server-side at that point so the distinction survives even if the user-facing copy stays generic.

title: The API boundary mixes snake_case and camelCase for the same field on the same resource, so GET /api/v3/domains returns created_at while POST returns createdAt, and the shared ScheduleItem type declares two field names the API never sends
category: inconsistent naming at the API boundary
description:
Some routes hand back database rows verbatim and some map them to camelCase, and a few do both in the same file.

app/api/v3/domains/route.ts is the clearest case. GET at :29-42 selects `id, domain, team_id, status, verification_method, created_at, verified_at, last_checked_at, last_check_error` and spreads the row, so the client receives snake_case. POST at :127-137 returns the same resource with `createdAt: row.created_at`. A third branch, the already-exists path at :103-115, returns neither. components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx has to bridge all three: its DomainItem interface at :34-50 mixes snake_case (team_id, verification_method, created_at, verified_at, last_checked_at, last_check_error) with camelCase (verificationRecordName, verificationRecordValue), and its optimistic insert at :147-150 writes `team_id: null, verification_method: "dns_txt", created_at: data.createdAt ?? new Date().toISOString()`, hand-translating the POST shape into the GET shape and inventing the fields POST does not send.

The schedules pair has already cost a visible bug. app/api/v3/schedules/route.ts:28 selects `last_run_at, next_run_at`, but components/profile/types.ts:185-186 declares ScheduleItem with `last_run` and `next_run`, names no endpoint returns. components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:121-132 works around it at runtime with a comment that states the problem: "The schedules API returns `next_run_at` / `last_run_at` ... but the shared ScheduleItem type ... declares `next_run` / `last_run`. Read both spellings so 'when does this run' isn't silently blank because of a mismatch in a type this component doesn't own." The fix is a `sch as unknown as Record<string, string | null | undefined>` cast that reads `record[which] ?? record[`${which}_at`]`, which defeats the type entirely.

The scale: 46 client-side files declare 491 snake_case interface fields (largest: components/admin/types.ts 97, components/admin/notifications/notifications-manager.tsx 63, components/profile/types.ts 37, components/teams/teams-types.ts 18). Against that, four routes do map: app/api/v3/history/[id]/route.ts returns `scannedAt: scan.scanned_at`, app/api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/shares/route.ts returns `userId: r.user_id`, app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts returns `sessionId: r.session_id`, app/api/v3/account/discord/route.ts returns `discordId`. So GET /api/v3/support-tickets returns raw `created_at` rows while its own sub-resource GET /api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/shares returns camelCase, to the same component.
impact: A client cannot assume a casing and has to check per endpoint, which is why one component ships a runtime dual-read cast and another hand-builds a snake_case row from a camelCase response. The ScheduleItem type is actively lying: TypeScript accepts `sch.next_run` and it is always undefined, so the compiler cannot catch the bug the cast works around. Any renaming of a database column also becomes a breaking public API change on the routes that spread rows, because the column name is the wire format.
recommendation: Do not attempt a repo-wide conversion. Fix the two provable cases: make POST /api/v3/domains return `created_at` like its own GET (app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:132) so components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:150 can drop the translation, and correct components/profile/types.ts:185-186 to `last_run_at` / `next_run_at` so the cast at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:126-132 can be deleted. Then write the rule down in app/docs/api (rows are returned as stored, snake_case, since that is what 491 declarations already assume) and convert the four camelCase-mapping routes to match, rather than converting the majority.

title: GET /api/version still does its own GitHub release fetch even though lib/updater/github-release.ts was extracted specifically to stop it, and the two have already drifted on timeout, caching and the release-url key name
description:
lib/updater/github-release.ts:1-8 states its purpose: "Kept separate so app/api/version/route.ts and the admin updater routes can share the same 'ask GitHub about a release' code instead of each doing its own fetch + JSON shape assumptions." It exports fetchLatestRelease(), whose githubJson() helper (:52-62) uses a 10 second timeout and `cache: "no-store"` with the comment "Never serve a stale cached release when the admin explicitly asked to check for or apply an update."

app/api/version/route.ts does not import it. It fetches VERSION_CHECK_URL itself at :11-16 with `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` and `next: { revalidate: 3600 }`, then re-implements toRelease's tag parsing at :34-38 (`tag_name.replace(/^v/, "")` and the `html_url || RELEASES_URL/tag/tagName` fallback). It does import the other extracted piece, compareVersions from lib/updater/version-compare.ts, which is what the admin route's own comment (app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts:22-24) points at when it says the two "never disagree".

They already differ on three axes: timeout 5,000 ms vs 10,000 ms; cache one-hour ISR revalidation vs no-store; and the output key `release_url` (app/api/version/route.ts:40, :52 and the no-op branch at :25) vs `releaseUrl` (app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts:56 and :70) for the same value. `release_url` is also the only snake_case key that route emits, next to camelCase-free flat fields.

/api/version is not internal: it is the public unauthenticated version endpoint the browser extension calls (extension/src/lib/api.ts:200, typed at extension/src/lib/types.ts:199) and it is documented in app/docs/api and lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md.
impact: A self-hosted operator can see two different answers to "is there an update" depending on which surface they look at, because the public endpoint can serve an hour-stale GitHub response while the admin panel never caches. Any future change to how a release is parsed (pre-release filtering, draft handling, a tag-format change, a GitHub API version bump) is applied in lib/updater/github-release.ts and silently missed on the endpoint the extension and the docs point at. The extension only reads `current` today, so the naming split is not currently breaking it.
recommendation: Rewrite app/api/version/route.ts's GET to call fetchLatestRelease() from lib/updater/github-release.ts and drop its inline fetch and tag parsing, keeping the route's own `next: { revalidate: 3600 }` behaviour by adding an optional cache mode argument to githubJson rather than a second fetch. Rename the response key to `releaseUrl` to match app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts, keeping `release_url` as a duplicate key for one release since it is a documented public field.

title: The anonymous demo scan abandons runAsyncChecks after its 15 s race, leaving the work and an uncleared timer running with no accounting
description: app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:215-219 builds `const asyncPromise = runAsyncChecks(url)` and races it against `new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(() => resolve([]), asyncChecksTimeoutMs))` (SCAN_ASYNC_CHECKS_TIMEOUT_MS default 15000, lib/config/config-values.ts:566). When the timeout wins, the handler returns but asyncPromise keeps executing -- runAsyncChecks fans out the full live-fetch battery (~23 exposed-file probes per lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:2724, plus GraphQL, bucket-listing and header probes) against the anonymous caller's chosen target with nothing left holding a reference to it. The timeoutPromise's setTimeout is never cleared, so the timer survives to its full 15 s even when the checks finish first. Contrast lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:573-647, which keeps `asyncTimeoutHandle` and clears it in a finally.
impact: The one endpoint reachable with no account at all can leave outbound probe batteries running past the response, so the visible per-IP demo budget (5 per 12 hours) understates the real outbound volume, and slow targets accumulate detached work in the shared process. Bounded in practice by the per-fetch AbortSignal timeouts inside the checks, which is why this is low rather than higher.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts, hold the timeout handle and clearTimeout it after the race (as lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:647 does), and pass an AbortSignal into runAsyncChecks that is aborted when the timeout wins so the abandoned branch actually stops issuing requests.

title: GET /api/v3/host/[hostname] and the badge endpoints are unauthenticated with no rate limiter, so the public-scan corpus can be scraped for free
description: app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts has no getSession call and no checkRateLimit import; its GET at :70 runs two Postgres queries per request -- a host_reputation lookup at :88-103 and, when source_scan_id is set, a scan_history lookup at :140 -- and returns the full findings JSONB plus result_meta. app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/trend/route.ts, app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts and app/api/v3/whoami-ip/route.ts are in the same position (no session, no limiter), while the sibling public listing endpoint app/api/v3/public-scans/route.ts:48-51 does gate on `public-scans:${ip}` and documents per-IP as "the only throttle available" for exactly this shape of route.
impact: An anonymous caller can enumerate hostnames at line rate and pull the complete finding set for every publicly-listed scan, and each request costs two DB round trips plus a JSONB serialisation from a connection pool shared with the scan workers. It is free compute and free bulk export of the product's differentiating dataset, with no per-IP ceiling to make it slow. Low rather than higher because the data is public by design and both queries are indexed point lookups.
recommendation: Apply the same `checkRateLimit({ key: \`public-scans:${ip}\`, ...RATE_LIMITS.publicScans })` gate used in app/api/v3/public-scans/route.ts:48 to app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts, its /trend sibling and app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts (use the /64-masked key from abuse-08 so it is not trivially rotated).

title: Signup returns 409 for a registered email and 200 for an unregistered one, handing back the enumeration oracle login and password-reset close
description: app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:147-150 does `const existing = await getUserByEmail(email); if (existing) return ApiResponse.conflict(ERROR_MESSAGES.DUPLICATE_EMAIL);` -- a deterministic 409-vs-200 split on whether an address has an account. The rest of the auth surface works hard to avoid exactly this: login returns one generic 401 for both 'no user' and 'wrong password' and burns a dummy scrypt hash to equalize timing (app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:78-86), forgot-password always returns the same 'If an account with that email exists' message (forgot-password/route.ts:64-76), and resend-verification returns the same string on all three outcomes (resend-verification/route.ts:221-236). The route's own comment at lines 124-128 names the problem ('an attacker who rotates IPs via residential proxy can enumerate which emails are registered (409 "already in use" vs 200 success differentiates them)') and answers it with a per-email limit of 5 per hour at line 130 -- which does not remove the oracle at all, because the FIRST request for any address already answers the question. The per-IP `signup:${ip}` bucket is 5 per 15 minutes, so a single residential-proxy pool tests thousands of addresses a day.
impact: Every enumeration defense elsewhere in the auth surface is nullified: an attacker confirms which of a scraped address list has VulnRadar accounts by posting each one to /signup once, then targets those addresses with credential stuffing or phishing that names the product. For a security-tools vendor, the membership list itself ('who at $COMPANY uses a vulnerability scanner') is the interesting output.
recommendation: Make signup answer identically for both cases: on a duplicate email, return the same 200 `SUCCESS_MESSAGES.SIGNUP` + `requiresVerification: true` body the new-account path returns, and instead of creating a row, send the existing account an 'someone tried to sign up with your address, sign in or reset your password' email. Keep the per-email bucket as flood control. The signup form then always shows 'check your email', and the real disambiguation happens in the inbox, which only the address owner can read.

title: Turning 2FA off leaves device_trust rows intact, so a previously trusted device skips the second factor when 2FA is turned back on
description: app/api/v3/auth/2fa/disable/route.ts:56-59 clears `totp_enabled`, `two_factor_method`, `totp_secret`, and `backup_codes`, and app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-setup/route.ts:332-338 (DELETE) clears the first two plus email_2fa_codes -- neither deletes from device_trust. Rows written by upsertTrustedDevice (lib/auth/device-trust.ts:89-116) live for DEVICE_TRUST_DAYS, default 30 (lib/config/config-values.ts:266), and findTrustedDevice (line 14) only checks `user_id + device_fingerprint + expires_at > NOW()`. So a device trusted on day 1, with 2FA disabled on day 2 and re-enabled on day 3, still satisfies the trusted-device bypass at app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:187, app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:369, and app/api/v3/auth/discord/callback/route.ts:278 for the remaining 27 days. The two other places that rotate a credential do get this right and explicitly say why: app/api/v3/auth/reset-password/route.ts:231 and app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:348 both `DELETE FROM device_trust WHERE user_id = $1` alongside the session wipe, with a comment about not leaving a planted trust row behind.
impact: A user who turns 2FA off and back on -- the documented way to re-enroll a new authenticator app, since app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:51-55 refuses to re-enroll while 2FA is active -- believes they have started clean. Any browser that was trusted before, including one an attacker had transient access to, keeps skipping the prompt. The trusted-devices UI (app/api/v3/auth/trusted-devices/route.ts) will list it, but nothing prompts the user to look there during re-enrollment.
recommendation: Add `await pool.query("DELETE FROM device_trust WHERE user_id = $1", [session.userId])` to app/api/v3/auth/2fa/disable/route.ts right after the UPDATE at line 56, and to the DELETE handler in app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-setup/route.ts after line 332 -- matching what reset-password and the password-change path already do.

title: Changing the account email leaves every other session and trusted device alive, unlike the password change in the same handler
description: PATCH /api/v3/auth/update treats email and password as the same class of 'sensitive change' at line 68 and gates both behind the same re-auth + `profile-reauth` bucket (lines 70-115). The two branches then diverge. The password branch at lines 337-356 calls deleteAllSessions(), deletes every device_trust row, mints a fresh session, and tells the user 'All other sessions have been signed out for security'. The email branch at lines 207-216 runs `UPDATE users SET email = $1, email_verified_at = NULL` plus sendEmailVerification and stops -- no session wipe, no device_trust wipe. The address the account's password-reset, 2FA email codes, and every security notification are delivered to has just changed identity, and every session that existed a moment earlier is still valid.
impact: An attacker who has a session plus the password (or, for an OAuth-only account, just the session -- lines 116-122 skip the password check entirely there) repoints the account to their own address and keeps every device they were signed in on. The legitimate owner is notified at both addresses (lines 224-247), but if they respond by changing the password they will not think to also check active sessions, and the attacker's own session is not what gets killed. It is also an internal inconsistency: the handler's own comment at lines 201-206 explains that email change is an account-takeover vector, then does not apply the mitigation it applies one branch down.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts, after the email UPDATE at line 207, run the same three statements the password branch runs at lines 343-356: `deleteAllSessions(session.userId)`, `DELETE FROM device_trust WHERE user_id = $1`, then `createSession(...)` and set the refreshed cookie (the code at lines 393-400 can be lifted into a small helper shared by both branches), and return the same `sessionInvalidated: true` flag so the client shows the same message.

title: The two Stripe setup routes hand-roll an exact role === "admin" check, bypassing requireAdmin's 2FA enforcement and locking out super_admin
description: app/api/v3/stripe/setup-products/route.ts:24-36 does getSession() then `if (session.role !== STAFF_ROLES.ADMIN) return 403`, and app/api/v3/stripe/setup-webhook/route.ts:27-38 does getSession() then a raw `SELECT role FROM users` compared against the string literal "admin". Neither goes through lib/auth/authorization.ts's requireAdmin(), so neither runs passesTwoFactorEnforcement (:138): with ENFORCE_STAFF_2FA on, an admin account with totp_enabled false is refused everywhere else in the admin surface but can still call both of these and write to the live Stripe catalog (products.create / prices.create at setup-products:85 and :112) and create a live Stripe webhook endpoint (setup-webhook:85). The exact-string comparison also excludes super_admin, which every other admin route accepts via STAFF_ROLE_HIERARCHY - AUDIT-011#drift-21 noted that half; the 2FA-enforcement half is separate and unfiled.
impact: The one class of account the ENFORCE_STAFF_2FA toggle is meant to neutralise retains write access to the production Stripe catalog and webhook configuration. Low rather than medium because the caller is still a genuine admin and the operations are near-idempotent, but it is the same bypass pattern as authz-06 and it sits on the billing integration.
recommendation: Replace the hand-rolled checks in both files with `const admin = await requireAdmin(); if (!admin) return ApiResponse.forbidden(...)` from lib/auth/authorization.ts. That fixes the 2FA bypass and the super_admin lockout in one change, and removes the duplicate `SELECT role FROM users` in setup-webhook/route.ts:32.

title: Scan screenshots are readable with no authentication at all, and by sequential legacy id, via the middleware's Bearer-token bypass
description: app/api/v3/scan/screenshot/[id]/route.ts:38 sets `authorized = scan.is_public === true` and only falls back to a session + getTeamResourceAccess check when that is false. scan_history.is_public defaults to true (instrumentation.ts:2190), so most rows qualify. The route is not in PUBLIC_PATHS, but middleware.ts:325 lets any request through when `authorization` merely starts with "Bearer " - the string is never validated there, and this route never validates it either (it only calls getSession()). So `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' https://host/api/v3/scan/screenshot/42` reaches the handler with no identity at all. resolveScanRow (lib/history/resolve-scan.ts:59-67) still matches a legacy numeric primary key alongside the opaque public_id, so the id space is `1..N` sequential. Every sibling per-scan route requires an authenticated owner or team-read (history/[id]/route.ts:117-166, history/[id]/report/route.ts:134-144); this one does not.
impact: An anonymous caller can walk ids 1..N and harvest the stored page screenshot of every public scan, and confirm which scan ids exist. The images are of publicly reachable sites so the content is low-sensitivity, but for a security product it is an unauthenticated enumeration of other tenants' scan activity, and it defeats the opaque public_id the rest of the codebase moved to precisely to stop id-walking.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/scan/screenshot/[id]/route.ts, require a session before the is_public shortcut (move the `getSession()` call above :38 and 404 when there is none), so the public surface stays the token-scoped app/api/v3/shared/[token]/screenshot route it already documents at :19-21. If truly anonymous access is wanted, at minimum reject the legacy numeric id here by calling scanNumericId and only accepting a public_id match.

title: matchesPathPattern compiles an admin-set notification path filter to `.*` per `*` and runs it in every visitor's browser, the same backtracking shape as the robots matcher
description: matchesPathPattern (lib/notifications/match-path.ts:12-22) escapes the regex metacharacters in an admin-configured `path_pattern`, replaces each `*` with `.*`, and evaluates `new RegExp(`^${escaped}$`).test(pathname)`. That is the identical construction to lib/scanner/crawl-discovery.ts:268-273 (inj-02) and has the same exponential worst case; the module comment says it is deliberately client-safe and used from both the bell dropdown and the site-wide banner renderer (components/shared/notification-center.tsx, components/shared/site-notifications.tsx), so it executes in every visitor's browser on every route change.
impact: An admin (or anyone who gains an admin session, or a compromised staff account) can set a notification targeting pattern such as `/a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*b` that hangs the main thread of every signed-in visitor's tab. Bounded because the input is admin-only, and there is no cross-tenant consequence, but it is an unnecessary self-inflicted foot-gun in shipped client code.
recommendation: Replace the regex in lib/notifications/match-path.ts with a linear greedy wildcard walk (split on `*`, then advance through pathname with indexOf, anchoring the first and last segments), or reject patterns containing more than two `*` characters in the admin notification form before they are stored.

title: The scheduled-scans plan limit is a read-then-insert with no guard, so concurrent POSTs let a user exceed their plan's scheduledScans cap
description: POST /api/v3/schedules counts existing rows with `SELECT COUNT(*)::int as count FROM scheduled_scans WHERE user_id = $1` (app/api/v3/schedules/route.ts:134-137), compares it against planLimits.scheduledScans via withinPlanLimit at :139-147, and then does an unguarded `INSERT INTO scheduled_scans ...` at :167-173. There is no row lock, no unique constraint, and no conditional INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit, so two requests that both read the same count before either inserts both pass the gate. The same shape exists for the team seat cap at app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:190-205 (count, then INSERT at :214) and the team-count cap at app/api/v3/teams/route.ts:78-91. Contrast lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts, which closes exactly this race for the scan counter with a single guarded upsert (`ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE rate_limits."count" < $2`, :366-368).
impact: A user (or a script) firing N parallel schedule-create requests lands N schedules where the plan allows one more, permanently over the cap until someone notices -- and each extra schedule then runs forever as an unmetered scan source (see logic-01). Bounded by how many requests overlap the same read, and self-limiting because the cap is re-read on the next single request, so the practical overshoot is small. The same argument applies to the team seat cap, where the overshoot is a paid-seat count.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/schedules/route.ts, replace the count-then-insert with a single data-modifying statement: `INSERT INTO scheduled_scans (...) SELECT $1, $2, ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scheduled_scans WHERE user_id = $1) < $limit RETURNING id`, treating a zero-row result as the over-limit rejection (skip the WHERE entirely when the limit is -1). Apply the same shape to the seat check in app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:190 and the team-count check in app/api/v3/teams/route.ts:78.

title: The staff plan floor applied on cancellation hardcodes three of the seven staff roles and omits super_admin, so those accounts drop to 'free' instead of their granted floor
category: duplicated role list drifted from its source of truth
description: Three separate cancellation paths reset the plan with the same hand-written CASE: `plan = CASE WHEN role IN ('admin', 'moderator', 'support') THEN 'pro_supporter' ELSE 'free' END` -- app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:640 (customer.subscription.deleted), app/api/v3/billing/subscription/cancel/route.ts:74 (immediate cancel), and app/api/v3/billing/route.ts:425 (cancel_immediately action). The canonical staff-role list is STAFF_ROLES in lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:22-30, which contains seven roles: admin, moderator, support, billing, security_analyst, content_manager, ops. The CASE covers three of them and, separately, super_admin -- whose granted floor is elite_supporter, not pro_supporter (lib/billing/staff-plan.ts:49, 62-64) -- is in none of the lists. lib/billing/staff-plan.ts's grantStaffPlan/revokeStaffPlan, which own this policy, are not called from any of the three cancel paths.
impact: A billing/security_analyst/content_manager/ops staffer who cancels a real paid subscription has users.plan written to 'free' rather than the pro_supporter floor their role grants. Their enforced limits are mostly unaffected because getUserPlan (lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:89) tags any STAFF_ROLES member as 'staff' and every resolver substitutes pro_supporter, so this is mainly a wrong displayed plan. A super_admin is the real case: super_admin is deliberately excluded from STAFF_ROLES (:20-21), so getUserPlan falls through to the literal column and returns 'free' -- that account is genuinely dropped to the Free tier's 25 scans/day and free-tier caps after canceling, until the next process restart, when reconcileStaffPlans (lib/billing/staff-plan.ts:253) sweeps it back to elite_supporter (and only if pre_staff_plan is still NULL).
recommendation: Replace the three inline CASE expressions with a call to the module that owns the policy: after the UPDATE that clears the Stripe columns, call grantStaffPlan(userId, role) from lib/billing/staff-plan.ts (exported already), or at minimum parameterise the CASE against STAFF_ROLES plus super_admin rather than a hardcoded triple -- e.g. `plan = CASE WHEN role = 'super_admin' THEN 'elite_supporter' WHEN role = ANY($n::text[]) THEN 'pro_supporter' ELSE 'free' END` with STAFF_ROLES bound as the array.

title: A lapsing Stripe subscription revokes the premium badge even when an active admin gift still entitles the user to it
category: entitlement revoked without checking the other grant path
description: The premium badge has two independent grant paths. The Stripe path calls grantPremiumBadge/revokePremiumBadge from lib/billing/badges.ts. The gift path awards it directly in app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:1674-1691 (SELECT the 'premium' badge id, INSERT INTO user_badges if absent) when an admin runs gift_subscription. revokePremiumBadge (lib/billing/badges.ts:32-48) is an unconditional `DELETE FROM user_badges WHERE user_id = $1 AND badge_id = $2` -- it never looks at gifted_subscriptions. It is called from customer.subscription.updated whenever the resolved plan is free (app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:583), from customer.subscription.deleted (:649), and from confirmSubscription (app/actions/stripe.ts:335). The symmetric case is handled correctly in the other direction: revoke_gift only removes the badge when the user is on the free plan (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:1709-1721).
impact: A user who has both an active admin gift and a Stripe subscription that then lapses, is canceled, or expires loses the premium badge even though the gift is still live and still grants them the paid plan. The badge is user-visible on shared scans, public scans and the profile (the badges query in app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:114-119 reads user_badges directly), so the account silently stops being marked as a supporter while still holding a valid gifted subscription. Nothing re-grants it: the gift path only inserts at gift creation, so the badge stays missing until an admin re-issues the gift.
recommendation: Make revokePremiumBadge in lib/billing/badges.ts conditional on there being no other live entitlement: guard the DELETE with `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM gifted_subscriptions WHERE user_id = $1 AND revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW())`, which mirrors the check revoke_gift already makes in the opposite direction at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:1709. That keeps all three Stripe callers (webhooks :583, :649 and app/actions/stripe.ts:335) correct without changing any of them.

title: 117 of the 155 API routes bypass the ApiResponse/withErrorHandling helpers and hand-roll five different error body shapes
description: lib/api/api-utils.ts already provides the canonical pieces: ApiResponse (:13-65) emits `{ error, status }` with a matching HTTP status for every 4xx/5xx class, and withErrorHandling (:263-274) converts an uncaught throw into `console.error("[API Error]", error)` plus a fixed `"An unexpected error occurred"` 500. Only 38 of the 155 route.ts files under app/api reference either one; the other 117 build responses with bare NextResponse.json, and 47 route files contain no `catch` at all. The result is five distinct error shapes in production: `{ error }` (bare NextResponse.json, the majority of the 233 `error:`-keyed literals), `{ error, status }` (ApiResponse), `{ success: false, error }` (21 occurrences, e.g. app/api/v3/webhooks/route.ts:299-303 and app/api/v3/stripe/setup-products/route.ts:148-152), `{ error, details, statusCode }` (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:287-294), and `{ message }` (app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:298). The shared client only understands one of them: lib/api/client.ts:46-49 reads `errorData.error` and otherwise falls back to the literal string `API error: <status>` set at :44, so a `{ message }` response surfaces to the user as "API error: 400".
impact: Client code cannot render a reliable message without knowing which route it called, which is how bare status strings end up in front of users. The 47 handler-less routes also mean an unexpected throw is formatted by Next.js rather than by the app, so those responses do not carry the `{ error }` key the client expects at all.
recommendation: Adopt ApiResponse as the single error constructor and wrap every handler in withErrorHandling. Do it in batches by directory rather than one sweep. Start with the five shape outliers named above so the client's single `errorData.error` read in lib/api/client.ts:46 is always satisfied.

title: The admin alert webhook that every escalation path depends on defaults to empty and has no test-delivery path, so an operator cannot know it works until an incident
description: sendAdminAlert (lib/admin/alert-webhook.ts:40-44) begins `const url = await getSetting("ADMIN_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL"); if (!url) return;` and the default is the empty string (lib/config/config-values.ts:429, registered at lib/config/registry.ts:2783). Every push signal in the app routes through it: the five worker escalators via lib/admin/failure-escalation.ts:100, and the boot-time schema, stale-scan and missing-table alerts at instrumentation.ts:139, :184, :198, :3491, :3531, :3631. Grepping ADMIN_ALERT_WEBHOOK across app/, components/ and lib/ finds only the config registry entries and alert-webhook.ts itself: there is no route, button, or admin action that sends a test alert, and the delivery failure paths (:50-56 for an unsafe URL, :86-90 for a non-2xx response) only console.error into a log the operator would have to already be reading.
impact: An operator who pastes a Slack or PagerDuty URL into the setting has no way to confirm it works. A typo, a revoked Slack webhook, or a URL that validateScanTarget (:47) now rejects produces a silent no-op, and the first time they find out is the incident the alert existed for. Until it is configured at all, the app has no push signal of any kind, which is the state a fresh install ships in.
recommendation: Add a "Send test alert" action next to the ADMIN_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL setting that calls sendAdminAlert with a `severity: "warning", event: "test_alert"` payload and surfaces the delivery result (including the non-2xx status from :87) in the UI rather than only in console.error. Have sendAdminAlert return a boolean instead of void so the caller can report it.

title: Two archival and delivery tables are written on every event and read by nothing
description: webhook_deliveries (instrumentation.ts:2328) is written on every attempt at lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:111 and never SELECTed; its index on (webhook_id, attempted_at DESC) is shaped for a UI that was never built. Already recorded as AUDIT-009 #185 and still open. admin_audit_log_archive (lib/database/audit-log-archive.ts:47) is created and INSERTed at :89, and a repo-wide grep returns only that file.
impact: A user whose webhook is failing has no way to see why, despite the data being captured. Purged compliance history is unviewable by any screen, route or export, which undermines the point of archiving it.
recommendation: Add a delivery log to Profile > Developer > Webhooks and an 'Archived batches' view to Admin > System > Audit Log. Both are read-only views over data that already exists.

title: Webhook signing secrets cannot be rotated, unlike API keys
description: webhooks.secret (instrumentation.ts:2313) is returned once at creation (app/api/v3/webhooks/route.ts:123) and the only UPDATE (app/api/v3/webhooks/[id]/route.ts:215) cannot set it. API keys have both rotate and revoke routes.
impact: A leaked webhook secret can only be addressed by deleting the webhook and recreating it, which breaks the consumer's configuration.
recommendation: Add a rotate path and a 'Rotate signing secret' control, mirroring the API key flow.

title: API keys silently 403 from a new network because bound_ip is never shown and cannot be reset
description: api_keys.bound_ip (instrumentation.ts:382) is enforced under API_KEY_IP_BINDING_ENABLED and auto-pins on first use (lib/api/api-keys.ts:213-266, :234). getUserApiKeys at :615-626 does not select it, no component references it, and there is no reset path.
impact: When the feature is enabled, a key that worked yesterday starts returning 403 from a new network with no visible cause and no way to fix it short of issuing a new key.
recommendation: Show the bound IP on the API keys list and add a 'Reset binding' action.

title: Seven client-sent fields are ignored by their handlers, one of them silently discarding user-chosen support categories
description: app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:15-21 defines CATEGORY_LABELS for bug, feature, security, help and staff_application, then :109 does CATEGORY_LABELS[category] || "Other". The form offers nine (components/contact/contact-types.ts:27-82); billing (:58), enterprise (:64) and feedback (:76) are POSTed verbatim and land in the support inbox labelled 'Other'. Others: source: "bulk" sent at app/dashboard/page.tsx:753 while app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:374 computes source itself, so bulk scans are recorded as ordinary Web scans; authenticated and staff query params sent by components/shared/notification-center.tsx:293-296 and components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:683-686 to a route that derives both from the session and never reads searchParams, with the comment at site-notifications.tsx:678-682 now actively wrong in claiming they are enforced server-side; message_type hardcoded by mass-email-manager.tsx:132 and never read; userId in the 2FA verify body (components/auth/login-2fa-form.tsx:70,72) deliberately not destructured; baseUrl in the AI-config save (profile-ai-settings-tab.tsx:115,139) used only as an equality check, so sending it can only ever produce a 400.
impact: The contact one is the only one with real user cost: triage information the user explicitly selected is discarded, and three categories are indistinguishable from 'Other' in the support inbox.
recommendation: Add billing, enterprise and feedback to CATEGORY_LABELS - a one-line fix. Delete the dead params and the incorrect comment at site-notifications.tsx:678-682.

title: lib/billing/billing.ts is a fully dead file, including the old Stripe Checkout Session flow deleted elsewhere this session
description: getUserPlan is superseded by lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts's staff-role/gifted-subscription-aware version. The same file's createSubscriptionCheckout has zero callers anywhere except its own test suite, already true before this session. The real live checkout path is app/actions/stripe.ts; billing.ts just never got the same cleanup as the Elements-based route deleted this session.

title: checkRateLimit uses epoch-aligned fixed windows, so a caller gets up to 2x the cap across a bucket boundary
description: lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:127-128 quantises the bucket to `Math.floor(now.getTime() / windowMs) * windowMs` and the UPSERT at :137-144 counts against `UNIQUE (key, window_start)`. This is a fixed window, not a sliding one, so a caller who spends the full cap in the last instant of one bucket and the full cap in the first instant of the next gets 2 x maxAttempts within one window's duration. For login that is 10 attempts inside 15 minutes rather than 5 (lib/config/config-values.ts:457-458); for demo scans, 10 anonymous scans inside a 12-hour span. The quantisation itself is deliberate and fixes a worse bug the comment at :120-126 describes (N requests in 1 ms creating N distinct buckets), so this is the residual, well-understood trade-off rather than a regression. Noted for the record: the limiter is correctly fail-CLOSED (a pool.query rejection propagates out of checkRateLimit and every caller's try/catch or withErrorHandling turns it into a 5xx, never an allowed request), the store is Postgres and therefore survives deploys and multiple instances, and getDailyRequestCount at lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:157 reads `window_start >= CURRENT_DATE` while every writer uses `date_trunc('day', NOW())` -- consistent only while the database session timezone is UTC.
impact: Doubles the effective burst on every named limit at bucket boundaries. Matters most for the login and 2FA-verify gates, where the per-account counters (`login-fail:${user.id}`) are the real defence and this is the outer layer.
recommendation: If tightening is wanted, move checkRateLimit to a two-bucket weighted sliding window: read the current and previous bucket counts in the same statement and reject when `prev * (1 - elapsed/windowMs) + curr >= maxAttempts`. Otherwise document the 2x boundary behaviour next to the bucketStart comment so the shipped numbers are read as ceilings of 2x, and pin the database session to UTC so the CURRENT_DATE / date_trunc pair cannot diverge.

title: Staff OIDC validates the ID token's issuer against the discovery document's own claim, not against the configured issuer URL
description: verifyStaffOidcIdToken calls `jwtVerify(idToken, jwks, { issuer: doc.issuer, audience: config.clientId })` at lib/auth/staff-oidc.ts:127-130, where `doc` is whatever came back from `${STAFF_OIDC_ISSUER_URL}/.well-known/openid-configuration` (getDiscoveryDocument, line 64). `doc.issuer` is never compared against `config.issuerUrl`, and getDiscoveryDocument's own validation at lines 82-86 checks only that authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, and jwks_uri are present -- issuer is not in that list even though it is declared required on the DiscoveryDocument interface at line 51. OIDC Discovery 1.0 section 4.3 requires the returned `issuer` to exactly match the issuer used to build the discovery URL, precisely so this check is not circular. The rest of the flow is sound: the nonce is bound through a short-lived httpOnly cookie (app/api/v3/auth/staff-oidc/route.ts:168), state is HMAC-signed, and the callback never creates or promotes an account (callback lines 87-92).
impact: No exploitable path today: reaching the vulnerable condition requires the admin-configured STAFF_OIDC_ISSUER_URL to serve a discovery document naming a different issuer and pointing jwks_uri at that issuer's keys, which means the admin already pointed staff SSO at a hostile endpoint. Worth fixing because it is the one place in an otherwise careful OIDC implementation where the trust anchor is self-asserted, and because the interface already declares the field required while the validation does not check it.
recommendation: In lib/auth/staff-oidc.ts getDiscoveryDocument (line 82), add `doc.issuer` to the required-fields check and reject when `doc.issuer.replace(/\/+$/, "") !== base`, so the discovery document must self-identify as the issuer the admin configured before any of its endpoints are used.
